If we say it was present, then its disappearance would entail the disappearance of the eternal, and that would close the door to proving the origination of the world. Allah knows best.
* * *
[Page 37]
The third issue: his saying ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾ is a plural form with the definite article (al-lam al-ta'rif), and by its apparent meaning it is for comprehensive inclusion (istighraq). Then there is no dispute that its apparent meaning is not what is intended, because many of the disbelievers embraced Islam. We therefore know that God may speak in a general form while meaning a specific group. This may be either because the indication that the general wording meant that specific group was clear at the time of the Messenger (ﷺ), so it was acceptable since there was no confusion and the intended meaning was evident. An example of this: if a person in a town has a particular group of enemies, and he says, "People are harming me," everyone understands that by "people" he means that specific group in particular. Or it may be because speaking in general terms in order to mean the specific is permissible, even if the explanation is not attached to it, according to those who allow delaying the explanation of a specification beyond the time of the address. Once this is established, it becomes clear that it is not possible to rely on any of the forms of generality with certainty that the reference is comprehensive, because it is possible that what is meant by them is the specific, and the indication of that was clear at the time of the Messenger (ﷺ), and so it was acceptable. The most that can be said is: had this indication existed, we would have known it, and since we do not know it, we know it did not exist. But this argument is weak, because inferring non-existence from non-finding is among the weakest indications that produce even conjecture, let alone certainty. Once this is established, it becomes clear that the Mu'tazilah's reliance on the general statements of threat to establish certainty of punishment is extremely weak. Allah knows best. Some Mu'tazilah tried to avoid this by saying: his saying "Indeed, those who disbelieve will not believe" is like the contradiction of his saying "Indeed, those who disbelieve will believe." The statement "Indeed, those who disbelieve will believe" is not true unless every one of them believes. When it is established that the affirmative case requires generality, it must follow that the negative case does not depend on generality. Rather, its truth is sufficed by the fact that faith does not proceed from any one of them, for whenever not one of that group believes, it is established that faith did not proceed from them. Thus it is established that his saying "Indeed, those who disbelieve will not believe" suffices, when applied to its apparent meaning, for it to be that not one of them believes. So how much more so when many of them do not believe? The answer: his saying ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾ is a plural form, and his saying ﴿will not believe﴾ is also a plural form. When a plural is paired with a plural, the individual is distributed over the individual. So its meaning is that each one of them does not believe, and in that case the aforementioned argument returns.
* * *
The fourth issue: the exegetes differed about who is meant here by ﴿those who disbelieve﴾. Some said they are the obstinate leaders of the Jews, whom God described as concealing the truth while knowing it. This is the view of Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father). Others said rather the intended are a group of the polytheists, such as Abu Lahab, Abu Jahl, al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, and their likes, those who denied after the clear proof and rejected after recognition. A parallel to this is God's saying ﴿Most of them turned away, so they do not hear﴾ and ﴿They say: "Our hearts are in coverings from what you invite us to"﴾ [41:4-5]. The peace of God be upon him was eager that all his people should believe, so God said to him ﴿Perhaps you would destroy yourself with grief over their traces if they do not believe in this message﴾ [18:6], and said ﴿Would you then compel people until they become believers?﴾ [10:99]. Then He, glorified and exalted, made clear to him (peace be upon him) that they would not believe, in order to cut off his hope in them and so that he would not be distressed because of it, for despair is one of the two comforts.
* * *
As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾, there are several issues:
(The first issue): The author of al-Kashshaf said: ﴿sawa'﴾ is a noun meaning equality (al-istiwa'), and it is described by it as it is described by verbal nouns (masadir). From it is His saying: ﴿Come to a word that is equal (sawa') between us and you﴾ [3:64], and ﴿in four days, complete (sawa') for those who ask﴾ [41:10], meaning "equal" (mustawiyah). So it is as if it were said: "Indeed, those who disbelieve, your warning and its absence are equal for them."
(The second issue): Regarding the case of ﴿sawa'﴾, there are two views. The first: its case-ending (irtifa') is because it is the predicate of inna, and ﴿whether you warned them or did not warn them﴾ is in the position of the raised (marfu') subject of it, as the doer (fa'il). It is as if it were said: "Indeed, those who disbelieve, your warning and its absence are equal for them," just as you say: "Indeed, Zayd, his brother and his paternal cousin are disputing." The second: ﴿whether you warned them or did not warn them﴾ is in the position of the subject (mubtada'), and sawa' is its predicate placed first, meaning "your warning and its absence are equal for them," and the sentence is the predicate of inna. Know that the second view is preferable, because sawa' is a noun, and treating it as a verb would be abandoning the apparent form without necessity, and that is not permissible. Given this, we say: it is known that what is meant is describing the warning and its absence as equal, so sawa' must be the predicate, and therefore the predicate comes first. This shows that placing the predicate before the subject is permissible. A parallel is His saying ﴿Equal (sawa'an) is their living and their dying﴾ [45:21]. Sibawayh transmitted the sayings "Tamimi am I" and "hated is the one who hates you." As for the Kufans, they do not permit this, and they argued for their position in two ways. The first: the subject is a thing (dhat), and the predicate is an attribute (sifah), and the thing precedes the attribute in terms of entitlement, so it must precede it in wording, by analogy with the followers in i'rab (grammatical case), the common cause being the non-independent status of the follower in meaning. The second: the predicate must contain a pronoun, so if the predicate were placed before the subject, the pronoun would appear before its referent, and that is not permissible, because a pronoun is a word that points to a known matter, so before knowing it, pointing to it is impossible, and thus pronominalization before mention is absurd. The Basrans answered the first argument by saying: what you have mentioned requires that the subject's precedence be preferred, not that it be obligatory. As for the second: pronominalization before mention occurs in Arabic speech, as in the saying "In his house the judge is sought," and God said ﴿Musa sensed fear within himself﴾ [20:67]. Zuhayr said:
Whoever meets him one day in his troubles, though aged, will find from him generosity and open-handedness as his disposition.
Allah knows best.
* * *
(The third issue): They agreed that the verb cannot be the subject of a predication (la yukhbaru 'anhu), because whoever says "went out hit" has not produced a coherent sentence. Some of them criticized this on several grounds. The first: His saying ﴿whether you warned them or did not warn them﴾ is a verb, and a predication has been made about it with His saying ﴿It is the same for them﴾. A parallel to this is His saying ﴿Then it occurred to them, after they had seen the signs, that they should imprison him for a time﴾ [12:35], where the doer of "occurred" (bada) is "that they should imprison him" (layasjununnahu).

[Page 38]

Secondly: The thing spoken of as being a verb must itself be a verb, so the verb has been described as a verb. If it is said: "The thing described as a verb is that word, and that word is a noun," we reply: In that case, if the thing described as a verb is not a verb but a noun, this statement is false. The correct position is that the thing described as a verb either is a noun or is not. If it is the first, the statement is false, because a noun cannot be a verb. If it is a verb, then the verb has become the subject of the statement.

Thirdly: When we say, "The verb is not spoken of," we have spoken of it by saying that it is not spoken of. If the subject of this statement were a noun, it would follow that we had spoken of a noun as not being spoken of, and that is an error. If it is a verb, then the verb has become the subject of the statement.

Then these people said: Since it is established that there is no impediment to speaking of a verb, there is no need for us to abandon the apparent meaning. As for the majority of the grammarians, they have agreed that it is not permissible to speak of a verb. Therefore the implied meaning is: "It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them." If it is objected: A departure from the literal meaning to the figurative must have some added benefit, either in meaning or in wording. What is the benefit here? We reply: The words of God, ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or you do not warn them﴾, mean: "It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them after this." For the people had reached such a degree of obstinacy, stubbornness, and turning away from the signs and proofs that no hope of their accepting in any way remained in them at all. Before that they were not like this. Had He said, "It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them," it would not have indicated that this state had arisen at this time and not before. But when He said, ﴿Whether you warn them or do not warn them﴾, it indicated that this condition had arisen at this time. So this indicates the arising of despair and the cutting off of hope from them, and we have already shown that this is the aim of this verse.

* * *

(Fourth issue): The author of the Kashshaf (al-Zamakhshari) said: The hamzah and "am" are both used merely for the meaning of interrogation, and the meaning of interrogation has been completely stripped from them. Sibawayh said: This has taken the form of the interrogative particle just as the vocative particle takes its form, as in His saying, "O God, forgive us, O company" (ayyatuha al-'isabah). He means that this takes the form of a question while not being a question, just as that takes the form of a call while not being a call.

(Fifth issue): In His words, ﴿a-anzarta-hum﴾ there are six recitations: either with two definite hamzahs with an alif between them, or without an alif between them; or with the first hamzah strong and the second between-between (bayn bayn), with an alif between them or without; and with the deletion of the interrogative particle, or with its deletion and the transfer of its vowel to the preceding consonant, as in the reading "qad aflaha." If it is asked: What do you say about one who changes the second into an alif? The author of the Kashshaf said: He is a grammatical solecist, outside the speech of the Arabs.

(Sixth issue): Warning (al-indhar) is the instilling of fear of God's punishment through restraining from disobedience. Warning was mentioned rather than good news (al-bishara) because the influence of warning on doing and abstaining is stronger than the influence of good news, since a person's preoccupation with averting harm is greater than his preoccupation with acquiring benefit. This is a place of emphasis, so mentioning warning is more fitting.

* * *

As for His words, ﴿they will not believe﴾, there are two issues:

(First issue): The author of the Kashshaf said: This is either a sentence emphasizing the sentence before it, or it is the predicate of "inna," with the sentence before it being a parenthetical insertion.

(Second issue): The people of the Sunnah (ahl al-sunnah) have argued from this verse and everything similar to it, such as His words, ﴿Certainly the word has come true against most of them, so they do not believe﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:7], and His words, ﴿Leave Me with the one whom I created alone﴾ up to His words, ﴿I will overwhelm him with a steep ascent﴾ [al-Muddaththir 74:11, 17], and His words, ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾ [al-Masad 111:1], that it is a charge to do what cannot be done. The argument is this: God, exalted is He, has spoken about a specific person that he will never believe. If faith were to come from him, the truth of God's report would turn into falsehood, and falsehood is ugly according to the opponent. Doing what is ugly entails either ignorance or need, and both are impossible for God. What leads to the impossible is itself impossible. So faith coming from him is impossible, and charging him with it is charging him with the impossible. This is sometimes stated in the form of knowledge: God, exalted is He, having known that he will not believe, the arising of faith from him would entail that God's knowledge becomes ignorance, and that is impossible, and what entails the impossible is impossible. So the command is an assignment of the impossible.

We state this in a third way: The existence of faith is impossible to occur together with the knowledge of its non-existence, because knowledge is only knowledge if it corresponds to the known, and knowledge of non-faith corresponds only if non-faith occurs. So if faith existed together with knowledge of its non-existence, it would follow that faith would have both existence and non-existence together, and that is impossible. So the command to believe together with God's knowledge of non-belief is a command to combine two opposites, indeed a command to combine non-existence and existence, and all of this is impossible.

We state this in a fourth way: God charged those whom He reported would not believe with faith absolutely. Faith requires accepting God's truthfulness in everything He reports, and among what He reported is that they will never believe. So they have become charged with believing that they will never believe, and this is a charge to combine negation and affirmation.

We state this in a fifth way: God censured the disbelievers for trying to do something contrary to what God had reported, in His words, ﴿They want to change the words of God. Say: You shall not follow us; thus has God said before﴾ [al-Fath 48:15]. So it is established that intending to bring about what God has reported will not come into being is an intention to change the speech of God, and that is forbidden. Here God has reported about them that they will never believe, so attempting faith on their part would be an intention to change God's speech, and that is forbidden. Abandoning the attempt at faith would also be opposition to God's command, so blame would attach both to abandoning and to doing.

These are the arguments mentioned in this place, and this is the speech that demolishes the foundations of Mu'tazilism. The early and later scholars among the verifiers have relied upon it in refuting the principles of the Mu'tazilah and demolishing their rules. They have exerted themselves and striven to repel it, but they have produced nothing convincing. I will mention the greatest of what they said, with God's help and guidance.

The Mu'tazilah said: We have two positions regarding this verse.

The first position: Showing that it is not permissible for God's knowledge and God's report about non-belief to be an obstacle to belief. The second position: Showing the rational answer in detail.

As for the first position, they said: What indicates it are several points.

First: The Qur'an is full of verses indicating that there is no barrier preventing anyone from believing. He said, ﴿And what prevented the people from believing when the guidance came to them?﴾ [al-Isra 17:94], which is a denial expressed in the form of a question. And it is well known that if a man confines another in a house from which he cannot leave, and then says, "What prevented you from attending to my needs?", that would be considered reprehensible. Similarly, His words, ﴿And what would it be upon them if they believed?﴾ [al-A'raf 7:39], and His words to Iblis, ﴿What prevented you from prostrating?﴾ [al-A'raf 7:12], and Moses' words to his brother, ﴿What prevented you when you saw them going astray?﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:92], and His words, ﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe?﴾ [al-Inshiqaq 84:20], ﴿So what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder?﴾ [al-Muddaththir 74:49], ﴿May God pardon you! Why did you give them permission?﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:43], ﴿Why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you?﴾ [al-Tahrim 66:1]. Al-Sahib ibn 'Abbad said in a section he wrote on this subject: How can He command him to believe while He has prevented him from it? Or forbid him disbelief while He has driven him to it? How can He turn him away from faith and then say, ﴿Where are you turned?﴾ [al-Takwir 81:26]? He creates falsehood in them and then says, ﴿Where are you deluded?﴾? He brings disbelief into being in them and then says, ﴿Why do you disbelieve?﴾? He creates in them the confusion of truth with falsehood and then says, ﴿Why do you confuse the truth with falsehood?﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:71]? He turns them away from the path and then says, ﴿Why do you bar from the way of God?﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:99]? He places between them and faith a barrier and then says, ﴿And what would it be upon them if they believed?﴾? He leads them astray from right guidance and then says, ﴿Where then are you going?﴾ [al-Takwir 81:26]? He misguides them from the religion until they turn away, and then says, ﴿So what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder?﴾ [al-Muddaththir 74:49].

Second: God, exalted is He, said, ﴿Messengers as bearers of good news and as warners, so that people will have no argument against God after the messengers﴾ [al-Nisa 4:165], and He said, ﴿And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said: Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger so that we might follow Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced?﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:134]. When He made clear that He had left them no excuse except that He had removed it from them, then if His knowledge of their disbelief and His report of their disbelief were a barrier preventing them from faith, that would be among the greatest excuses and the strongest grounds to repel punishment from them. Since this is not the case, we know that it is not a barrier.

Third: God, exalted is He, related about the disbelievers in the surah "Ha Mim, the Prostration," that they said, ﴿Our hearts are under coverings against what you call us to, and in our ears is deafness﴾ [Fussilat 41:5], and God only mentioned that as a censure of them in this statement. So if knowledge were a barrier, they would have been truthful in this, so why did He censure them for it?

Fourth: God, exalted is He, revealed His words, ﴿Indeed those who disbelieve﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Baqarah 2:6], as a censure of them and a warning against disbelief and a denunciation of their act. So if they were prevented from faith, unable to attain it, they would not deserve censure at all, but would be excused, just as the blind man is excused for not walking.

Fifth: The Qur'an was sent down only to be a proof for God and His messenger against them, not for them to be a proof against God and against His messenger. So if knowledge and report were a barrier, they could say: If You know disbelief and are informed of it, then abandoning disbelief is impossible for us, so why do You seek the impossible from us and not command us with the impossible? It is well known that this is something for which God and His messenger have no answer, if it were established that knowledge and report prevent.

Sixth: His words, exalted is He, ﴿An excellent protector and an excellent helper﴾ [al-Anfal 8:40]. If, in the presence of a barrier to faith, one were charged with it, He would not be an excellent protector but a wretched protector, and it is well known that this is disbelief. They said: So it is established by these points that there is no barrier at all to faith and obedience, and therefore it is necessary to affirm with certainty that God's knowledge of non-belief and His report of its non-existence do not constitute a barrier to faith.

* * *

The second position: They said: What indicates that knowledge of non-belief does not prevent the existence of belief are several points.

First: If that were the case, it would necessarily follow that God would not be capable of anything, because that whose occurrence He knows must be necessary in occurrence, and that whose non-occurrence He knows must be impossible in occurrence. The necessary has no power over it, for if it is necessary in occurrence not by power, then whether power is present or not, it occurs necessarily, and what is like that has no effect of power in it. As for the impossible, there is no power over it. So it would follow that God, exalted is He, would not be capable of anything at all, and that is disbelief by consensus. Therefore it is established that knowledge of the non-existence of a thing does not prevent the possibility of its existence.

وثانيها: أنَّ العِلْمَ يتعلَّق بالمعلوم على ما هو عليه، فإن كان مُمكنًا كان علمُه مُمكنًا، وإن كان واجبًا كان علمُه واجبًا. ولا شكَّ أنَّ الإيمانَ والكفرَ بالنظر إلى ذاتِهما مُمكنا الوجود، فلو صار واجبَ الوجودِ بسبب العلم كان العلمُ مؤثِّرًا في المعلوم، وقد بيَّنّا أنَّ ذلك مُحال.

وثالثها: لو كان الخبرُ والعلمُ مانعًا لَما كان العبدُ قادرًا على شيءٍ أصلًا؛ لأنَّ الذي علِمَ اللهُ تعالى وقوعَه كان واجبَ الوقوع، والواجبُ لا قدرةَ عليه؛ والذي علِمَ عدمَه كان ممتنعَ الوقوع، والممتنعُ لا قدرةَ عليه. فوجب ألّا يكونَ العبدُ قادرًا على شيءٍ أصلًا، فكانت حركاتُه وسكناتُه جاريةً مجرى حركاتِ الجمادات، والحركاتِ الاضطراريةِ للحيوانات. لكنّا نعلم بالبديهة فسادَ ذلك؛ فإن رمى إنسانٌ إنسانًا بالآجُرّة حتى شجَّه، فإنّا نذمُّ الرامي ولا نذمُّ الآجُرّة، ونُدرِك بالبديهة تفرقةً بين ما إذا سقطت الآجُرّةُ عليه، وبين ما إذا لكمَه إنسانٌ بالاختيار. ولذلك فإنَّ العقلاء ببداءةِ عقولهم يُدرِكون الفرقَ بين مدحِ المُحسِن وذمِّ المُسيء، ويلتمسون ويأمرون ويُعاتِبون ويقولون: لِمَ فعلتَ ولِمَ تركتَ؟ فدلَّ على أنَّ العلمَ والخبرَ غيرُ مانعٍ من الفعلِ والترك.

ورابعها: لو كان العلمُ بالعدم مانعًا للوجود، لكان أمرُ الله تعالى للكافر بالإيمان أمرًا بإعدام علمِه. وكما أنه لا يليق به أن يأمر عبادَه بأن يُعدِموه، فكذلك لا يليق به أن يأمرهم بأن يُعدِموا علمَه؛ لأنَّ إعدامَ ذاتِ الله وصفاتِه غيرُ معقول، والأمرُ به سَفهٌ وعبث. فدلَّ على أنَّ العلمَ بالعدم لا يكون مانعًا من الوجود.

وخامسها: أنَّ الإيمانَ في نفسه من قبيل الممكنات الجائزات نظرًا إلى ذاته وعينه، فوجب أن يعلمه الله تعالى من الممكنات الجائزات؛ إذ لو لم يعلمه كذلك لكان ذلك العلمُ جهلًا، وهو مُحال. وإذا علِمه الله تعالى من الممكنات الجائزات التي لا يمتنع وجودُها وعدمُها البتّةَ، فلو صار بسبب العلم واجبًا، لزم أن يجتمعَ على الشيء الواحد كونُه من الممكنات، وكونُه ليس من الممكنات، وذلك مُحال.

وسادسها: أنَّ الأمرَ بالمُحال سَفهٌ وعبث، فلو جاز ورودُ الشرع به لجاز ورودُه أيضًا بكلِّ أنواع السَّفه، فما كان يمتنعُ وروده بإظهار المعجزة على يد الكاذبين، ولا إنزالِ الأكاذيب والأباطيل. وعلى هذا التقدير لا يبقى وثوقٌ بصحة نبوةِ الأنبياء ولا بصحةِ القرآن، بل يجوز أن يكون كلُّه كذبًا وسفهًا. ولَمّا بطل ذلك علمنا أنَّ العلمَ بعدمِ الإيمان والخبرَ عن عدمِ الإيمان لا يمنعُ من الإيمان.

وسابعها: أنه لو جاز ورودُ الأمرِ بالمُحال في هذه الصورة لجاز
[صفحة ٤٢]
ورودُ أمرِ الأعمى بنَقْطِ المصاحف، والمُزمِنِ بالطيرانِ في الهواء، وأن يُقال لمن قُيِّدت يداه ورجلاه وأُلقي من شاهقِ جبل: لِمَ لا تطير إلى فوق؟ ولَمّا لم يجُز شيءٌ من ذلك في العقول، علِمنا أنه لا يجوز الأمرُ بالمُحال، فثبت أنَّ العلمَ بالعدم لا يمنعُ من الوجود.

وثامنها: لو جاز ورودُ الأمرِ بذلك لجاز بعثةُ الأنبياء إلى الجمادات، وإنزالُ الكتب عليها، وإنزالُ الملائكة لتبليغِ التكاليف إليها حالًا بعد حال، ومعلومٌ أنَّ ذلك سخريةٌ وتلاعبٌ بالدين.

وتاسعها: أنَّ العلمَ بوجود الشيء لو اقتضى وجوبَه، لأغنى العلمُ عن القدرة والإرادة، فوجب ألّا يكونَ اللهُ تعالى قادرًا مريدًا مختارًا، وذلك قولُ الفلاسفة القائلين بالمُوجِب.

وعاشرها: الآياتُ الدالةُ على أنَّ تكليفَ ما لا يُطاق لم يُوجَد، قال الله تعالى: ﴿لا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إلّا وُسْعَها﴾ [البقرة: ٢٨٦]، وقال: ﴿وما جَعَلَ عَلَيْكم في الدِّينِ مِن حَرَجٍ﴾ [الحج: ٧٨]، وقال: ﴿ويَضَعُ عَنْهم إصْرَهم والأغْلالَ الَّتِي كانَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ [الأعراف: ١٥٧]. وأيُّ حرجٍ ومشقةٍ فوق التكليفِ بالمُحال؟

* * *

المقامُ الثالثُ: الجوابُ على سبيلِ التفصيل. وللمعتزلة (Mu'tazila، أي أهل الاعتزال، وهم أصحاب المذهب العقلي في علم الكلام) فيه طريقان:

الأول: طريقةُ أبي عليٍّ (الجُبّائي) وأبي هاشمٍ والقاضي عبدِ الجبّار، فإنّا لمّا قلنا: لو وقع خلافُ معلومِ الله تعالى لانقلبَ علمُه جهلًا، قالوا: خطأٌ قولُ من يقول: إنه ينقلب علمُه جهلًا، وخطأٌ أيضًا قولُ من يقول: إنه لا ينقلب، ولكن يجب الإمساكُ عن القولين.

والثاني: طريقةُ الكعبيِّ واختيارُ أبي الحسينِ البصريّ: أنَّ العلمَ تبعٌ للمعلوم، فإذا فرضتَ الواقعَ من العبد من الإيمان عرفتَ أنَّ الحاصلَ في الأزل لله تعالى هو العلمُ بالإيمان، ومتى فرضتَ الواقعَ منه هو الكفرُ بدلًا عن الإيمان عرفتَ أنَّ الحاصلَ في الأزل هو العلمُ بالكفر بدلًا عن الإيمان، فهذا فرضُ علمٍ بدلًا عن علمٍ آخر، لا أنه تغيَّر العلم. فهذان الجوابان هما اللذان عليهما اعتمادُ جمهور المعتزلة.

واعلم أنَّ هذا المبحثَ صار منشأً لضلالاتٍ عظيمة: فمنها أنَّ مُنكِري التكاليف والنبوّات قالوا: قد سمعنا كلامَ أهلِ الجبر (Jabr، أي القول بالجبر والإلزام القدري) فوجدناه قويًّا قاطعًا، وهذان الجوابان اللذان ذكرهما المعتزلة يجريان مجرى الخرافة، ولا يلتفت العاقل إليهما، وسمعنا كلامَ المعتزلةِ في أنَّ مع القولِ بالجبر لا يجوز التكليفُ ويُقبَّح، والجوابُ الذي ذكره أهلُ الجبر ضعيفٌ جدًّا، فصار مجموعُ الكلامين كلامًا قويًّا في نفي التكاليف، ومتى بطل ذلك بطل القولُ بالنبوات. ومنها أنَّ الطاعنين في القرآن قالوا: الذي قالَه المعتزلةُ من الآياتِ الكثيرةِ الدالةِ على أنه لا مَنعَ من الإيمان ومن الطاعة فقد صدقوا فيه، والذي قالَه الجبريةُ من أنَّ العلمَ بعدم الإيمان مانعٌ عنه فقد صدقوا فيه، فدلَّ على أنَّ القرآنَ ورد على ضدِّ العقل وعلى خلافه، وذلك من أعظم المطاعن وأقوى القوادح فيه. ثم مَن سلَّم من هؤلاء أنَّ هذا القرآنَ هو القرآنُ الذي جاء به محمدٌ ﷺ توسَّل به إلى الطعن فيه. وقال قومٌ من الرافضة (Rafida، إحدى فرق الشيعة): إنَّ هذا الذي عندنا ليس هو القرآنَ الذي جاء به محمدٌ، بل غُيِّر وبُدِّل. والدليلُ عليه اشتمالُه على هذه المناقضاتِ التي ظهرت بسبب هذه المناظرة الدائرةِ بين أهلِ الجبر وأهلِ القدر (Qadar، أي القائلين بحرية الإرادة الإنسانية). ومنها أنَّ المقلِّدةَ الطاعنين في النظر والاستدلال احتجّوا بهذه المناظرة وقالوا: لو جوَّزنا التمسكَ بالدلائل العقلية لزم القدحُ في التكليف والنبوّة بسبب هذه المناظرة، فإنَّ كلامَ أهلِ الجبر في نهاية القوة في إثبات الجبر، وكلامَ أهل القدر في بيان أنه متى ثبت الجبرُ بطل التكليفُ بالكلية في نهاية القوة، فيتولَّد من مجموع الكلامين أعظمُ شبهةٍ في القدح والتكليف والنبوة، فثبت أنَّ الرجوعَ إلى العقليات يُورث الكفرَ والضلال، وعند هذا قيل: مَن تعمَّق في الكلام تزندق (صار زنديقًا). ومنها أنَّ هشامَ بنَ الحكم زعم أنه سبحانه لا يعلم الأشياءَ قبل
[صفحة ٤٣]
وقوعِها، وجوَّز البداءَ (bada'، أي تغيُّر الرأي والظهور لعلمٍ جديد) على الله تعالى، وقال: إنَّ قولَه: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَواءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أأنْذَرْتَهم أمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهم لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ إنما وقع على سبيل الاستدلال بالأمارة، ويجوز له أن يُظهِر خلافَ ما ذكره، وإنما قال بهذا المذهب فِرارًا من تلك الإشكالاتِ المتقدمة.

واعلم أنَّ جملةَ الوجوهِ التي رويناها عن المعتزلة كلماتٌ لا تعلُّقَ لها بالكشف عن وجه الجواب، بل هي جاريةٌ مجرى التشنيعات. فأما الجوابانِ اللذان عليهما اعتمادُ القوم ففي نهاية الضعف. أما قولُ أبي عليٍّ وأبي هاشمٍ والقاضي: خطأٌ قولُ من يقول إنه يدل، وخطأٌ قولُ من يقول إنه لا يدل، إن كان المرادُ منه الحكمَ بفساد القسمين كان ذلك حكمًا بفساد النفي والإثبات، وذلك لا يرتضيه العقل، وإن كان معناه أنَّ أحدَهما حقٌّ، لكن لا أعرف أنَّ الحقَّ هو أنه يدل أو لا يدل، كفى في دفعه تقريرُ وجه الاستدلال، فإنّا لَمّا بيَّنّا أنَّ العلمَ بالعدم لا يحصل إلا مع العدم، فلو حصل الوجودُ معه لكان قد اجتمع العدمُ والوجودُ معًا، ولا يتمكن العقل من تقرير كلامٍ أوضحَ من هذا وأقلَّ مقدماتٍ فيه. وأما قولُ الكعبي ففي نهاية الضعف، لأنّا وإن كنا لا ندري أنَّ الله تعالى كان في الأزل عالمًا بوجود الإيمان أو بعدمه، لكنّا نعلم أنَّ العلمَ بأحد هذين الأمرين كان حاصلًا، وهو الآنَ أيضًا حاضرٌ، فلو حصل مع العلم بأحد النقيضين ذلك النقيضُ الآخَرُ لزم اجتماعُ النقيضين، ولو قيل بأنَّ ذلك العلمَ لا يبقى كان ذلك اعترافًا بانقلاب العلم جهلًا. وهذا آخرُ الكلام في هذا البحث.

واعلم أنَّ الكلامَ المعنويَّ هو الذي تقدَّم، وبقي في هذا الباب أمورٌ أخرى إقناعية، ولا بد من ذكرها وهي خمسة:

أحدُها: روى الخطيبُ في كتاب تاريخ بغداد عن مُعاذِ بنِ مُعاذٍ العَنْبَريِّ، قال: كنتُ جالسًا عند عمرِو بنِ عُبيد، فأتاه رجلٌ، فقال: يا أبا عثمانَ، سمعتُ واللهِ اليومَ بالكفر! فقال: لا تُعجِّلْ بالكفر، وما سمعتَ؟ قال: سمعتُ هاشمًا الأوقصَ يقول: إنَّ ﴿تَبَّتْ يَدا أبِي لَهَبٍ﴾ [المسد: ١] وقولَه: ﴿ذَرْنِي ومَن خَلَقْتُ وحِيدًا﴾ [المدثر: ١١] إلى قوله: ﴿سَأُصْلِيهِ سَقَرَ﴾ [المدثر: ٢٦] إنَّ هذا ليس في أمِّ الكتاب، والله تعالى يقول: ﴿حم﴾ ﴿والكِتابِ المُبِينِ﴾ [الدخان: ٢] إلى قوله: ﴿وإنَّهُ في أمِّ الكتابِ لَدَيْنا لَعَلِيٌّ حَكِيمٌ﴾ [الزخرف: ٤]، فما الكفرُ إلا هذا يا أبا عثمان. فسكت عمرٌو هُنَيْهةً ثم أقبل عليَّ فقال: واللهِ لو كان القولُ كما يقول، ما كان على أبي لهبٍ من لومٍ، ولا على الوليدِ من لومٍ. فلَمّا سمع الرجلُ ذلك قال: أتقولُ يا أبا عثمانَ ذلك؟ هذا واللهِ الذي قال مُعاذٌ! فدخل بالإسلام وخرج بالكفر. وحُكي أيضًا أنه دخل رجلٌ على عمرِو بنِ عُبيد، وقرأ عنده: ﴿بَلْ هو قُرْآنٌ مَجِيدٌ﴾ ﴿فِي لَوْحٍ مَحْفُوظٍ﴾ [البروج: ٢١-٢٢]، فقال له: أخبِرْني عن (تبَّتْ)، أكانت في اللوح المحفوظ؟ فقال عمرٌو: ليس هكذا كانت، بل كانت: تبَّتْ يدا مَن عمل بمثلِ ما عمل أبو لهبٍ. فقال له الرجل: هكذا ينبغي أن تُقرأ إذا قمنا إلى الصلاة! فغضب عمرٌو وقال: إنَّ علمَ اللهِ ليس بشيطانٍ، إنَّ علمَ اللهِ لا يضرُّ ولا ينفع. وهذه الحكايةُ تدل على شكِّ عمرِو بنِ عُبيد في صحةِ القرآن.

وثانيها: روى القاضي في كتاب طبقاتِ المعتزلة «عن ابنِ عمر، أنَّ رجلًا قام إليه، فقال: يا أبا عبدِ الرحمن، إنَّ أقوامًا يزنون ويسرقون ويشربون الخمرَ ويقتلون النفسَ التي حرَّم اللهُ إلا بالحقِّ ويقولون: كان ذلك في علمِ الله فلم نجد منه بُدًّا! فغضب ثم قال: سبحانَ اللهِ العظيم! قد كان في علمِه أنهم يفعلونها، فلم
[صفحة ٤٤]
يحملْهم عِلمُ اللهِ على فعلِها.
حدَّثني أبي عمرُ بنُ الخطاب، أنه سمع رسولَ اللهِ ﷺ يقول: مَثَلُ عِلمِ اللهِ فيكم كمَثَلِ السماءِ التي أظلَّتْكم، والأرضِ التي أقلَّتْكم، فكما لا تستطيعون الخروجَ من السماءِ والأرض، فكذلك لا تستطيعون الخروجَ من عِلمِ اللهِ تعالى، وكما لا تحملُكمُ السماءُ والأرضُ على الذنوب، فكذلك لا يحملُكم عِلمُ اللهِ تعالى عليها».

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 2, verse 6 (part 5 of 5):

Know that among the reports narrated by the Jabriyyah (determinists) and the Qadariyyah (those who affirm human free will) there are many. The purpose of narrating this hadith is to show that it is not fitting for the Messenger to say such a thing, because it is self-contradictory and corrupt. As for its self-contradiction, his saying, "And likewise you cannot escape from the knowledge of God," is explicit in determinism (jabr), while what precedes it is explicit in free will (qadar), so it is self-contradictory. As for its corruption, we have explained that knowledge of the non-occurrence of faith and the occurrence of faith are mutually exclusive. Therefore, imposing the obligation of faith while there is knowledge of its non-occurrence is an imposition of combining negation and affirmation. As for the heavens and the earth, they do not contradict any of the actions. It is therefore clear that comparing one of the two situations to the other proceeds only from an ignorant person or one who feigns ignorance, and the station of prophethood is far above such a thing.

Third: there are two well-known hadiths on this subject. As for the first hadith, it is what is narrated in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) from al-A'mash, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ), who is the truthful and the one whose word is confirmed, said: "Indeed, one of you is gathered in his mother's womb for forty days as a drop of semen, then he becomes a clinging clot likewise, then he becomes a lump of flesh likewise, then God sends to him an angel who breathes the spirit into him, and he is commanded with four words: he writes down his provision, his term, his deed, and whether he is wretched or happy. By God, other than whom there is no god, indeed one of you may act by the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is between him and it only a cubit, and then the Decree overtakes him and he acts by the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it. And indeed one of you may act by the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is between him and it only a cubit, and then the Decree overtakes him and he acts by the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it."

Al-Khatib (al-Baghdadi) related in Tarikh Baghdad, from Amr ibn Ubayd, that he said: "If I heard al-A'mash saying this, I would call him a liar. If I heard Zayd ibn Wahb saying this, I would not like it. If I heard Abdullah ibn Mas'ud saying this, I would not accept it. If I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) saying this, I would reject it. And if I heard God, Mighty and Majestic, saying this, I would say: 'You did not take our covenant upon this.'"

As for the second hadith, it is the debate between Adam and Moses, peace be upon them both. Moses said to Adam: "You are the one who made people wretched and expelled them from Paradise?" Adam said: "You are the one whom God chose for His messages and His speech, and He sent down the Torah to you. Do you find that God decreed it against me?" He said: "Yes." Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "So Adam overcame Moses in argument."

The Mu'tazilah criticized it in several respects:

The first: this report implies that Moses blamed Adam for a minor sin, and that implies ignorance on the part of Moses, peace be upon him, which is impermissible.

The second: how can a son address his father with harsh speech?

The third: he said, "You are the one who made people wretched and expelled them from Paradise," while Moses knew that the wretchedness of creation and their expulsion from Paradise did not come from Adam, but God Himself expelled him from it.

The fourth: Adam, peace be upon him, argued with something that is not a proof, for if it were a proof, then Pharaoh, Haman, and the rest of the disbelievers would have been able to argue with it. Since that is invalid, we know the corruption of this argument.

The fifth: the Messenger, peace be upon him, affirmed Adam's position in this matter, although we have explained that it is not correct.

When this is established, the hadith must be interpreted in one of three ways:

The first: he (peace be upon him) related this account from the Jews, not that he related it from God Most High or on his own authority. The Messenger, peace be upon him, had mentioned this narration, but the narrator, when he entered, heard only this statement, so he assumed that he (peace be upon him) had mentioned it on his own authority and not from the Jews.

The second: his saying "so Adam overcame" is in the accusative (fa-hajja Adama), meaning that Moses, peace be upon him, prevailed over him and made him the one overcome in argument, and that what Adam brought forward is neither a proof nor an excuse.

The third, which is the one relied upon: the purpose of the debate is not to blame him for disobedience, nor for excusing himself by God's knowledge. Rather, Moses, peace be upon him, asked him about the cause that led him to that slip, so that he was expelled from Paradise because of it. Adam said: "My expulsion from Paradise was not because of that slip, but because God Most High had written for me that I would leave Paradise for the earth and be a vicegerent in it. This meaning was written in the Torah. Therefore, Adam's argument was strong, and Moses, peace be upon him, became in that matter like one who is defeated."

Know that the discussion of this question is very long, and the Qur'an is full of it. We will examine the matter thoroughly in this commentary, if God Most High wills; and what we have mentioned here is sufficient.

[p. 45]

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 2, verse 7 (part 1 of 4)**

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Allah has sealed their hearts and their hearing, and over their eyes is a covering, and for them is a great punishment.﴾

Know that when Exalted is He, in the previous verse, made clear that they do not believe, He informed in this verse of the cause for which they did not believe, which is the sealing (al-khatm). The discussion here falls into several issues.

**The first issue:** al-khatm (sealing) and al-katm (concealing) are siblings, because in making something certain by stamping it with a seal there is a concealing of it and a covering over it, so that it cannot be reached or observed. Al-ghishawah (the covering) is the form fi'alah from ghashshahu, meaning he covered it, and this pattern denotes that which wraps around a thing, like the ʿişābah (headband) and the ʿimāmah (turban).

**The second issue:** The people have differed regarding this sealing. As for those who say that the actions of servants are created by Allah Exalted, their position on this statement is clear. Then they have two views. Some of them said: the sealing is the creation of disbelief in the hearts of the disbelievers. Others said: it is the creation of the motive (dāʿiyah) which, when joined to the capability (qudrah), makes the whole of the capability together with it a sufficient cause that necessitates the occurrence of disbelief. The exposition of this is that the one capable of disbelief is either capable of abandoning it or not capable. If he is not capable of abandoning it, then the capability to disbelieve necessitates disbelief, so the creation of the capability to disbelieve entails the creation of disbelief. If he is capable of abandoning it, then the relation of that capability to the act of disbelief and to its abandonment is equal. Then either its becoming the source of the act instead of abandonment depends on the joining of a determining factor (murajjih) to it, or it does not depend on it. If it does not depend on it, then a possible thing has occurred without a determining factor, and permitting this entails undermining the inference from the possible to the effecting cause, and that entails the denial of the Creator, which is impossible. And if it depends on a determining factor, then that determining factor is either from the act of Allah, or from the act of the servant, or neither from the act of Allah nor from the act of the servant. It is not permissible that it be from the act of the servant, otherwise an infinite regress (tasalsul) would follow. Nor is it permissible that it be neither from the act of Allah nor from the act of the servant, because that would necessitate the occurrence of a thing without an effecting cause, and that invalidates the claim of a Creator. Thus it is established that the servant's capability becoming the source of a specific object of capability depends on a determining factor being joined to it, which is from the act of Allah Exalted.

We say: when that determining factor is joined to that capability, then either the influence of the capability on that effect becomes necessary, or possible, or impossible. The second and third are invalid, so the first is determined. And we only said that it cannot be possible because if it were possible, it would be valid in the intellect that the whole of the capability together with that determining factor should sometimes occur with that effect and sometimes be separated from it. Let us assume that this occurs, because whatever is possible, its assumed occurrence does not necessitate an impossibility. Then that whole sometimes results in the effect and sometimes does not result in the effect. The specification of one of the two times, that the effect follows it, either depends on the joining of a further qualifier to it, or does not depend on it. If it depends on it, then the effecting cause is that whole together with this additional qualifier, not that whole alone, and we had assumed that the whole alone is self-sufficient, which refutes this. Also, the division recurs in this second whole. If it depends on another condition, an infinite regress follows, which is impossible. And if it does not depend on it, then that whole has occurred sometimes in a state in which it is a source of the effect and sometimes in a state in which it is not a source of it, while neither of the two times has been distinguished from the other by anything at all. So this would be a claim of the preponderance of the possible without a determining factor, which is impossible. Thus it is established that at the occurrence of that determining factor, it is impossible for the emergence of that effect to be possible. As for its not being impossible, this is evident, for otherwise the determining factor of existence would be a determining factor of non-existence, which is impossible. And when both divisions are invalidated, it is established that at the occurrence of the determining factor of existence, the effect is necessarily existent from the whole resulting from the capability and from that determining factor. When this is established, the doctrine of compulsion (jabr) becomes necessary, because before the occurrence of that determining factor the emergence of the act was impossible, and after its occurrence it is necessary. When you know this, the creation of the motive that necessitates disbelief in the heart is a sealing upon the heart and a prevention of it from accepting faith. For when He, glorified is He, ruled concerning them that they do not believe, He mentioned immediately after this what functions as the cause that necessitates it, because knowledge of the cause yields knowledge of the effect, and knowledge of the effect is not complete unless it is derived from knowledge of the cause. This is the view of whoever attributes all originated things to Allah Exalted.

As for the Muʿtazilah, they said: it is not permissible to apply this verse to the prevention from faith, and they argued for this with the arguments that we related from them in the first verse, and added here that Allah Exalted has rebuked the disbelievers who said that there was over their hearts a covering and veil that prevents them from faith: ﴿And they say: "Our hearts are uncircumcised"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 88], ﴿Rather, Allah has sealed them for their disbelief, so they do not believe except a few﴾ [al-Nisa': 155], and He said: ﴿So most of them turned away, and they do not hear﴾, ﴿And they say: "Our hearts are in coverings from what you call us to"﴾ [Fussilat: 4, 5]. All of this is a reproach and a condemnation from Allah Exalted of what they claimed, that they were prevented from faith. Then they said: rather, it is necessary to interpret the sealing and the covering as referring to other matters. Then they mentioned several aspects regarding it:

**The first:** When the people turned away and abandoned being guided by the signs of Allah Exalted, until that became for them like habit and nature, their condition resembled the condition of one who is prevented from something and hindered from it. Likewise, this was in their eyes, so that it was as if they were blocked and could see nothing, and as if there were deafness in their ears so that the reminder could not reach them. This was attributed to Allah Exalted because this attribute, in its firmness and the strength of its persistence, is like an innate thing. For this reason He Exalted said: ﴿Rather, Allah has sealed upon them for their disbelief, so they do not believe﴾ [al-Nisa': 155], ﴿Nay, rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 14], ﴿So He caused hypocrisy to follow in their hearts until the Day they meet Him﴾ [al-Tawbah: 77].

**The second:** A minimal cause suffices for the propriety of the attribution. So the devil is in reality the one who seals, or the disbeliever, but since Allah Exalted is the One who empowered him, He attributed the sealing to Him, just as an act is attributed to its cause.

**The third:** When they turned away from reflection and did not give ear to the reminder, and that occurred at the time when Allah Exalted presented them with proofs, what they did was attributed to Allah Exalted, because its occurrence coincided with His presenting His proofs to them. Like His saying in Surat Bara'ah: ﴿So it increased them in uncleanness to their uncleanness﴾ [al-Tawbah: 125], meaning they increased in disbelief through it, in addition to their disbelief.

**The fourth:** They reached such a degree of disbelief that no way remained for them to attain faith except through compulsion and coercion. But Allah Exalted did not leave them in that state, so that the obligation (taklif) would not be nullified. So He expressed the withholding of compulsion and coercion by the sealing, to indicate that they were the ones who had gone so far in disbelief that they would not desist from it except by force. This is the ultimate degree in describing their obstinacy in error.

**The fifth:** That this is a report of what the disbelievers used to say, mocking him: ﴿Our hearts are in coverings from what you call us to, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a veil﴾ [Fussilat: 5]. A parallel to this in reporting and mockery is His saying:
( ﴿Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not going to desist until there came to them the clear evidence﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 1].

**The sixth:** The sealing upon the hearts of the disbelievers from Allah Exalted is His testimony against them that they do not believe, and upon their hearts that they do not comprehend the reminder and do not accept the truth, and upon their hearing that it does not listen to the truth. This is like when a man says to his companion: "I want you to seal what so-and-so says," meaning: that you affirm it and bear witness that it is true. So Allah Exalted informed in the previous verse that they do not believe, and informed in this verse that He has witnessed this and preserved it against them.

**The seventh:** Some of them said: this verse came concerning specific people among the disbelievers, whom Allah Exalted subjected to this sealing and imprinting in this world as punishment for them in the immediate term, just as He hastened punishments in this world for many disbelievers. He said: ﴿And you have certainly known those among you who transgressed in the Sabbath, so We said to them: "Be apes, despised"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 65], and He said: ﴿So it is forbidden to them for forty years, wandering in the land. So do not grieve over the defiant people﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 26], and similar to this are the hastened punishments, for what Allah Exalted knew of their lesson for His servants and their benefit. So this would be like what was done to these people by way of sealing and imprinting, except that when they reach through it the state of not understanding, the obligation falls from them, just as it falls from one who has been transformed. And Allah has removed the obligation from one who has some intellect, like one who is near puberty. We do not deny that Allah may create in the hearts of the disbelievers an impediment that prevents them from understanding and reflection, when He knows that this is more beneficial for them, just as He may take away their minds and blind their eyes. But in this state they are not under obligation.

**The eighth:** It is permissible that Allah makes upon their hearts a sealing and upon their eyes a covering without that being a barrier between them and faith. Rather, that would be like the dullness a person finds in his heart, the speck in his eyes, and the ringing in his ear. Allah does all of that to them so as to constrict their chests and bring them distress and grief. So that would be a punishment that prevents faith, just as He did to the Children of Israel, so they wandered. Then this act occurs in some of the disbelievers, and that would be a sign and a proof for the Prophet (ﷺ), like the plague (rijz) that was sent down upon the people of Pharaoh until they cried out for relief from it. All of this is restricted to what Allah Exalted knows to be most beneficial for the servants.

**The ninth:** It is permissible that He performs this sealing upon them in the Hereafter, just as He has informed that He will make them blind. He said: ﴿And We shall gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind, mute, and deaf﴾ [al-Isra': 97], and He said: ﴿And We shall gather the criminals on that Day blue-eyed﴾ [Ta-Ha: 102], and He said: ﴿Today We seal upon their mouths﴾ [Ya-Sin: 65], and He said: ﴿For them therein is a roaring, and they therein do not hear﴾ [al-Anbiya': 100].

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 2, verse 7 (part 2 of 4):

The tenth view: what has been related from al-Hasan al-Basri, and which was chosen by Abu 'Ali al-Jubba'i and al-Qadi ('Abd al-Jabbar), is that the intended meaning is a mark and a sign that He places upon the hearts and hearing of the disbelievers, by which the angels deduce that they are disbelievers and that they will never believe. It is therefore not far-fetched that there may be in the hearts of the believers a sign by which the angels recognise that they are believers in the sight of God, as He said: ﴿Those, He has written faith upon their hearts﴾ [al-Mujadila: 22]. At that point the angels love him and seek forgiveness for him. And there is for the hearts of the disbelievers a sign by which the angels recognise that they are cursed in the sight of God, so they hate them and curse them. The benefit of that sign is either a benefit that returns to the angels, because once they know by that sign that he is a disbeliever cursed in the sight of God Almighty, this becomes a deterrent for them from disbelief. Or it returns to the responsible person (al-mukallaf), for when he knows that whenever he believes, the people of the heavens love him, this becomes an encouragement for him toward faith, and when he knows that whenever he commits disbelief the angels recognise this about him and so they hate him and curse him, this becomes a restraint for him from disbelief.

They said: "Sealing in this sense is not impossible, for we are able, after the book is sealed, to unseal it and read it. Moreover, sealing is in the same position as writing upon the forehead of the disbeliever that he is a disbeliever. If that does not prevent him from faith, then likewise this disbeliever is able to remove that mark from his heart by coming to faith and leaving disbelief."

They said: "The heart and the hearing were specified for this because the auditory proofs (al-adilla al-sam'iyya) are only obtained through hearing, and the rational proofs (al-adilla al-'aqliyya) are only obtained from the side of the heart. For this reason He mentioned the two specifically."

Page 48

If it is said: "Then should the veil over the sight also be understood in the sense of a sign?" We say: No. For we only interpreted what preceded as a stamp and a sign because the literal meaning of the language requires that, and there is nothing preventing it, so it was obligatory to affirm it. As for the veil (al-ghishawa), its literal meaning is a covering that prevents seeing, and it is known from the state of the disbelievers that the opposite of this is the case. Therefore it must be taken in a figurative sense, namely comparing their condition to the condition of one who does not benefit from his sight in the matter of guidance. This is the totality of what people have said on this point.

* * *

(Third issue): The expressions in the Qur'an close in meaning to sealing are: al-tab' (imprinting), al-kinan (coverings), al-rayn upon the heart (the rust/covering), al-waqr in the ears (heaviness/deafness), and al-ghishawa over the sight. Then the verses that come in this regard are of differing kinds. The first category: there is evidence for the occurrence of these things. He said: ﴿Nay, rather, what they have earned has rusted over their hearts﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 14]; ﴿And We have placed coverings upon their hearts lest they understand it, and in their ears a deafness﴾ [al-An'am: 25]; ﴿And their hearts were sealed﴾ [al-Tawba: 87]; ﴿Nay, Allah has sealed them for their disbelief﴾ [al-Nisa': 155]; ﴿So most of them turned away, and they do not hear﴾ [Fussilat: 4]; ﴿That he may warn whoever is alive﴾ [Ya-Sin: 70]; ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾ [al-Rum: 52]; ﴿They are dead, not living﴾ [al-Nahl: 21]; ﴿In their hearts is a disease﴾ [al-Baqara: 10].

The second category: there is evidence that there is absolutely no impediment: ﴿And what prevented the people from believing﴾ [al-Isra': 94]; ﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ [al-Kahf: 29]; ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾ [al-Baqara: 286]; ﴿And He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship﴾ [al-Hajj: 78]; ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah?﴾ [al-Baqara: 28]; ﴿Why do you mix the truth with falsehood?﴾ [Al 'Imran: 71]. The Qur'an is filled with these two categories, and each category became a support for a group. Thus the auditory proofs, because they come from both sides, fall within the sphere of contradiction. As for the rational proofs, they are those whose indication has already been pointed out. In sum, this issue is among the greatest of the Islamic issues, the most numerous in its branches, and the most severe in its disputes.

It is related that the Imam Abu al-Qasim al-Ansari was asked about the takfir (declaring unbelief) of the Mu'tazila in this issue, and he said: "No, because they have exalted Him (tanzih)." Then he was asked about the People of the Sunna (Ahl al-Sunna), and he said: "No, because they have magnified Him (ta'zim)." The meaning is that both groups sought only to affirm the majesty of God and the loftiness of His greatness. Except that the People of the Sunna fixed their gaze on greatness, and they said: "He must be the one who originates, and there is no originator other than Him." And the Mu'tazila fixed their gaze on wisdom, and they said: "It does not befit the majesty of His presence to have these abominations."

I say: Here there is another secret, which is that affirming God leads to the claim of compulsion (al-jabr), because if the act were not dependent upon a motive (da'iya), it would follow that a possible thing occurs without a determinant (murajjih), which is denying the Creator. And if it were dependent, it would follow that there is compulsion. Affirming the Messenger leads to the claim of power (al-qudra). Indeed, here there is another secret, which is above all of these: when we returned to the sound nature and the first intellect, we found that for that which existence and non-existence are equal in relation to, one of them is not preferred over the other except by a determinant. This requires compulsion. We also find an evident distinction between voluntary movements and involuntary movements, and a self-evident certainty about the goodness of praise and the ugliness of blame, and about commanding and forbidding. That requires the doctrine of the Mu'tazila. So this issue falls into the sphere of contradiction according to the necessary knowledges, and according to the speculative knowledges, and according to the magnification of God Most High with regard to His power and wisdom, and according to tawhid and tanzih, and according to the auditory proofs. Because of these sources that we have explained, and the secrets whose realities we have uncovered, the issue has become difficult, obscure, and grave. So we ask the Mighty God to grant us success in the truth, and to end our affair with good. Amin, Lord of the worlds.

* * *

(Fourth issue): The author of al-Kashshaf said: The wording allows that hearing may be included in the ruling of sealing and in the ruling of covering. However, the preferable view is that it is included in the ruling of sealing, due to His saying: ﴿And He has sealed upon their hearing and their hearts, and placed upon their sight a covering﴾ [al-Jathiya: 23], and because they pause upon "their hearing" but not upon "their hearts."

Page 49

(Fifth issue): The benefit of repeating the preposition in His saying ﴿and upon their hearing﴾ is that, since it was restated for the hearing, it is more indicative of the intensity of the sealing in both places.

(Sixth issue): Why He gathered the hearts and the sights, but made the hearing singular, is for several reasons:

First: He made the hearing singular because each one of them has one hearing, just as one says: "He brought me the heads of the two rams," meaning the head of each one of them. Just as He made the belly singular in the verse: "Eat from part of your belly, so that you may live." They do this when there is no confusion. When there is confusion, as when you say: "their horse" or "their garment," and you mean the plural, they avoid it.

Second: the hearing is originally a verbal noun (masdar), and verbal nouns are not pluralised. One says: "two men who fast" (rajulan sawm), and "men who fast" (rijal sawm), so the origin is observed. What indicates this is the plural of "ear" (udhun) in His saying: ﴿And in our ears is a heaviness﴾ [Fussilat: 5].

Third: that we estimate an omitted modifier, meaning: "and upon the faculties of their hearing."

Fourth: Sibawayh said: He made the word for hearing singular, but He mentioned what came before it and what came after it in the plural form, and that indicates that the intended meaning is also the plural. God Most High said: ﴿He brings them out from the darknesses into the light﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 16]; ﴿from the right and from the left﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 37]. The poet al-Ra'i said:

Upon them are the carcasses of the exhausted (camels), so their bones are white, but their hides are hard.

He meant their hides.

And Ibn Abi 'Abla read: [wa-'ala asma'ihim] (and upon their hearings, in the plural).

* * *

(Seventh issue): Some people said: Hearing is superior to sight, because God Most High, wherever He mentioned them, placed hearing before sight, and precedence is evidence of superiority. Also, hearing is a condition of prophethood, unlike sight, and for this reason He did not send a deaf messenger, although there were among them those afflicted with blindness. Also, through hearing the results of some people's intellects reach others, so hearing is as if it were a cause for the perfection of the intellect through knowledge, while sight only makes you aware of sensible things. Also, hearing acts in the six directions, unlike sight. Also, when hearing is lost, speech is lost, but when sight is lost, speech is not lost.

Others gave precedence to sight, because the instrument of the seeing faculty is more noble. Also, the object of the seeing faculty is light, while the object of the hearing faculty is air (rih).

Eighth issue: His saying ﴿God has sealed upon their hearts﴾ indicates that the locus of knowledge is the heart. We have fully explained this in His saying ﴿The trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 193–194], in Surat al-Shu'ara'.

(Ninth issue): The author of al-Kashshaf said: Sight is the light of the eye, which is that by which the seer sees and perceives visible things, just as insight (basira) is the light of the heart, which is that by which one discerns and reflects. It is as if they were two subtle substances, into which God Most High placed two instruments, for seeing and for discernment. I say: The Mu'tazila, his own companions, are not satisfied with this statement from him. A thorough account of the nature of seeing requires obscure investigations that are not suited to this place.

(Tenth issue): The word (ghishawa) has been read with a kasra and a fatha (ghishawatan), and ghushawatun with a damma and rafa', and ghashawatan with a fatha and nasb, and ghishwatun with a kasra and rafa', and ghashwatun with a fatha and rafa' and nasb, and 'ashawatun with an unpointed 'ayn and rafa', from al-'asha. The ghishawa is the covering, and from it comes al-ghashiya (the overwhelming). From it comes "he was overcome (ghushiya 'alayhi)" when his intellect departs. And al-ghashayan is a metaphor for intercourse.

(Eleventh issue): al-'adhab (punishment) is like al-nakal (exemplary punishment) in form and meaning, because you say: "a'dhaba 'anhu" when he refrained from it, just as you say "nakala 'anhu." From it comes al-'adhb (sweet water), because it quenches thirst and drives it away, unlike salt, which increases it. This is shown by their naming it nuqakh, because it breaks thirst (yanqakhu al-'atash), that is, breaks it, and furat, because it removes it from the heart. Then the term was extended so that every grievous pain is called 'adhab, even if it is not nakal, that is, a punishment by which the offender is restrained from returning to the offence. The difference between 'azim (great) and kabir (large): al-'azim is the opposite of al-haqir (contemptible), and al-kabir is the opposite of al-saghir (small), so that the 'azim is above the kabir, just as the haqir is below the saghir. Both are used for bodies and for events alike. One says: "a great man (rajul 'azim)" and "a large man (rajul kabir)," meaning his body or his importance. The indefiniteness (al-tankir) means that upon their sights is a kind of covering different from what people are accustomed to, namely the covering of blindness to the signs of God. And for them, among the great pains, there is a great kind whose true nature no one knows except God Most High.

* * *

(Twelfth issue): The Muslims agree that it is good for God Most High to punish the disbelievers. Some of them said: It is not good. They interpreted His saying ﴿and for them is a great punishment﴾ [al-Baqara: 7] as meaning that they deserve that, but His generosity obliges Him to pardon. Here we will mention the proofs of both groups. As for those who do not permit punishment, they have held to several matters:

First: that punishment is a harm free of any aspect of benefit, and therefore it must be ugly. That it is a harm there is no doubt. And that it is free of any aspect of benefit: because that benefit is either returning to God Most High or to other than Him. The first is false, because He, glorified be He, is exalted above benefit and harm, unlike one of us in the observable world. For when his servant wrongs him, he disciplines him, because he takes pleasure in that discipline on account of the love of vengeance in his heart; and because when he disciplines him, he will be restrained after that from what harms him.

The second is also invalid, because that benefit either returns to the one being punished or to someone else. If it returns to the one being punished, that is impossible, since harm cannot be the very same thing as benefit. If it returns to someone else, that is also impossible, because averting harm takes priority in consideration over conveying benefit. So inflicting harm on one person for the sake of conveying benefit to another person is preferring the lesser over the greater, and that is invalid. Moreover, there is no benefit that God, exalted is He, wishes to convey to anyone that He is not able to convey without the intermediary of harming another. So the intermediary of that harm would serve no purpose. It is therefore established that punishment is a harm empty of all aspects of benefit, and that its ugliness is known by the immediate judgement of reason. Indeed, its ugliness is more evident to minds than the ugliness of a lie that causes no harm, or of ignorance that causes no harm. Rather, its ugliness is greater than the ugliness of a harmful lie and of harmful ignorance, because that harmful lie is a means to harm, and the ugliness of what is a means to harm is less than the ugliness of harm itself. Once its ugliness is established, its issuing from God, exalted is He, is ruled out, because He is All-Wise, and the All-Wise does not do what is ugly.

Second: God, exalted is He, knew that the disbeliever would not believe, as He said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.﴾ Once this is established, it is established that whenever the disbeliever is obligated, nothing from him appears except disobedience. So if that disobedience were a cause for punishment, then that obligation would necessarily entail deserving punishment, either because it is the complete cause or because it is part of the cause. In general, that obligation is a matter such that, whenever it occurs, punishment inevitably follows it. And whatever entails harm empty of benefit is ugly. Therefore that obligation must be ugly, and the All-Wise does not do what is ugly. Nothing remains here except one of two options: either it is said that this obligation did not exist, or, if it existed, it does not entail punishment. Whichever way it is, the purpose is achieved.

Third: God, exalted is He, either it is said that He created creation for benefit, or for harm, or neither for benefit nor for harm. If He created them for benefit, then He must not obligate them with what leads to the opposite of His purpose, while knowing that it is so. And since He knew their insistence on disobedience, if He obligated them, the obligation would be an act leading them to punishment. So if He intends their benefit, He must not obligate them. Since He did obligate them, this shows that disobedience is not a cause for deserving punishment. It is not permissible to say that He created them neither for benefit nor for harm, because leaving them in non-existence would suffice for that. Also, on this assumption it would be purposeless. And it is not permissible to say that He created them for harm, because one such as this is not merciful or generous, and the intellects and the revealed laws agree that He is merciful and generous, and that He is the best of protectors and the best of helpers. All of this indicates the absence of punishment.

Fourth: He, glorified is He, is the Creator of the motives that cause disobedience, so He is the one who compels them to it, and thus it is ugly to punish for them. We said that He is the Creator of those motives because we have explained that the act proceeding from capacity depends on the joining of the motive that God, exalted is He, creates in it, and we have explained that this necessitates compulsion (al-jabr), and punishing the one compelled is ugly to the intellects. They have perhaps established this in another way, and said: If the commands and prohibitions of the Law have come to two people among mankind, and one of them accepted them while the other opposed them, so one was rewarded and the other was punished, then if it is asked, why did this one accept and that one oppose? It is said: because the one who accepted loved reward and feared punishment, so he obeyed, while the other did not love and did not fear, so he disobeyed; or because this one listened to the one who admonished him and understood his speech, so he obeyed, while that one did not listen and did not understand, so he disobeyed. Then it is said: and why did this one listen and understand, while that one did not listen and did not understand? We say: because this one is intelligent, prudent and perceptive, while that one is foolish, ignorant and dull. Then it is said: and why was this one singled out with prudence and perceptiveness rather than that one? There is no doubt that perceptiveness and dullness are innate conditions, for a person does not choose stupidity and foolishness, nor does he produce them in himself. So when causes end in matters that God, exalted is He, created by necessity, we know that all these matters are by the decree of God, exalted is He. It is not possible for you to equate the two persons, one of whom obeyed and the other disobeyed, in every respect, I mean in intellect and ignorance, shrewdness and dullness, prudence and foolishness, and in teachers, motivators and deterrents. Nor is it possible for you to say that if they were equal in all of that, they would not be equal in obedience and disobedience. Therefore, the cause of obedience and disobedience in persons is matters that came about by God's creation and decree, exalted is He. At this point it is said: where is justice, mercy and generosity in creating the disobedient one with the harshness and audacity, the stupidity and hardness, the recklessness and foolishness with which God created him, and then punishing him for it? Why did He not create him like He created the obedient one, intelligent, prudent, knowing and wise? And where is justice in heating his heart, strengthening his anger, inflaming his brain, increasing his recklessness, and not providing him with what He provided to others of a skilled educator, a knowledgeable teacher, and a preacher who conveys? Rather, He appoints for him the opposites of these in their actions and characters, so he learns from them, and then He takes him to account for what He takes the intelligent, prudent one to account for, the wise, knowledgeable one, cool-headed, of balanced temperament, gentle of spirit, to whom He gave a compassionate trainer and a perfect teacher? This is not in any way part of justice, mercy, generosity and kindness! Thus it is established by these aspects that the claim of punishment contradicts the dictates of reason.

Fifth: God, exalted is He, only obligated us with benefit for its return to us, because He said: ﴿If you do good, you do good for yourselves; and if you do evil, it is against yourselves.﴾ [Al-Isra', 17:7] So if we disobey, we have deprived ourselves of those benefits. Would it be good in the intellects that the All-Wise seizes a person and says to him: I will torment you with severe torment because you deprived yourself of some benefits? It is said to him: the attainment of benefit is outweighed in comparison to averting harm. Suppose I deprived myself of the lesser of the two objectives; would I then be deprived of the greater for that reason? Would it be good for a master to seize his slave and say: you were able to earn a dinar for yourself, to benefit from it alone, without my having any purpose at all in it; since you did not earn that dinar and did not benefit from it, I will seize you and cut your limbs to pieces? There is no doubt that this is the utmost folly. So how does this befit the Most Wise of judges?! Then they said: suppose we grant this punishment; from where comes the claim of its perpetuity? For the hardest-hearted of people, the most severe in harshness, rudeness and distance from good, if he seizes one who has gone to extremes in harming him, and tortures him for a day, a month or a year, he becomes sated with him and wearies of him; if he were to persist in it, everyone would blame him. And it is said: suppose he went to extremes in harming you, but until when is this torment? Either you kill him and relieve him, or you release him. If this is ugly from a human who delights in retaliation, then how does this perpetuity that is claimed befit the Self-Sufficient, who is independent of all?!

Sixth: He, glorified is He, forbade His servants from exceeding the measure, saying: ﴿So let him not exceed bounds in killing; indeed he is supported.﴾ [Al-Isra', 17:33] and He said: ﴿The recompense for an evil is an evil like it.﴾ [Ash-Shura, 42:40] Then, suppose the servant disobeyed God, exalted is He, throughout his life; where is his lifespan in relation to eternity? So perpetual punishment would be injustice.

Seventh: If the servant persisted in disbelief throughout his life, then repented and died, God would pardon him, answer his supplication and accept his repentance. Do you not see that this Generous and Great One, when those tormented have no intellects left, or their intellects have not remained in the Hereafter, why do they not repent of their sins? And when they repent, why does God, exalted is He, not accept their repentance, why does He not hear their call, and why does He frustrate their hope? Why was He in this world in such mercy and generosity that He said: ﴿Call upon Me, I will respond to you.﴾ [Ghafir, 40:60] ﴿Or who responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him?﴾ [An-Naml, 27:62], while in the Hereafter He has become such that the more humbly they supplicate to Him, the more He addresses them only with His words: ﴿Be silent therein, and do not speak to Me.﴾ [Al-Mu'minun, 23:108] They said: these aspects necessitate certainty of the absence of punishment. Then whoever among these believed in the Qur'an said: the excuse for what came in the Qur'an of various kinds of punishment is in several respects:

First: that clinging to verbal evidences does not produce certainty, while rational evidences produce certainty, and conjecture does not oppose certainty. We said that verbal evidences do not produce certainty because verbal evidences are built upon principles that are all speculative, and what is built upon the speculative is speculative. We said they are built upon speculative principles because they rest on the transmission of languages and the transmission of grammar and morphology, and the narrators of these things are not known to have reached the level of mass transmission (tawatur), so their transmission is speculative. Also, they rest on the absence of homonymy, the absence of metaphor, the absence of specification, the absence of ellipsis, the absence of addition and deficiency, and the absence of inversion and transposition, and all of these are speculative matters. Also, they rest on the absence of a rational counter-evidence; for if it existed, it would not be possible to say that both are true or both are false together, and it would not be possible to prefer transmission over reason, because reason is the basis of transmission, and impugning reason necessitates impugning both reason and transmission together. But the absence of a rational counter-evidence is speculative, if it is not found. So how much more so, since we have found here rational evidences contrary to these apparent meanings? Thus it is established that the indication of these transmitted evidences is speculative. As for the fact that the speculative does not oppose the certain, there is no doubt about it.

Second: that overlooking a threat is praiseworthy among people. A poet said:
"When I threaten someone or promise him, I break my threat, and I fulfil my promise."
Rather, insisting on carrying out the threat is regarded as baseness. And if this is so, it must not befit God, exalted is He. This is based on a point, which is that Ahl al-Sunnah (the people of the Sunnah) permitted the abrogation (naskh) of a command before the period of its fulfilment. The essence of their position on this is that a command is sometimes prescribed for a wisdom arising from the commanded act itself, and sometimes for a wisdom arising from the command itself. A master may say to his slave: do such-and-such an act tomorrow, even though he knows at present that he will forbid him from it tomorrow, and his aim in that command is that the slave should show submission to his master in that matter and train himself to obey him. Likewise, if God knows of the servant that he will die tomorrow, then according to Ahl al-Sunnah it is good to say: pray tomorrow if you live. The purpose of this command is not to achieve the commanded act, because that is impossible here; rather, the purpose is a wisdom arising from the command alone, namely the achievement of submission and obedience and the abandonment of rebellion. Since this is established...

[Page 53]

So we say: why should it not be permissible that a report (khabar) is likewise? Sometimes the source of wisdom in reports is the thing reported about, and that is in the case of promise (wa'd). Other times the source of wisdom is the report itself, not what is reported about, as in the case of threat (wa'id). Reports in the form of threat serve to deter from sins and to encourage acts of obedience. When this aim is achieved, it is permissible that what is reported about does not occur, as in the case of threat. At this point they said: God's promise of reward is a binding truth, but His threat of punishment is not binding. It was intended only for the welfare of the responsible persons (mukallafun), together with His all-encompassing mercy toward them. It is like the father who threatens his son with killing, blinding, cutting off, or beating. If the son obeys his command, he has benefited; and if he does not, the compassion in the father's heart prevents him from killing him or punishing him. If it is said: in all cases this would be a lie, and lying is ugly (qabih). We say: we do not grant that every lie is ugly; rather the ugly lie is the harmful lie, but the beneficial lie is not. Furthermore, even if we grant that, we do not grant that it is a lie. Is it not the case that all the general statements (umumat) of the Qur'an are specified (makhsusa), and that this is not called a lie? Is it not the case that all the ambiguous verses (mutashabihat) are turned away from their apparent meanings, and this is not called a lie? So likewise here.

Third: Is it not the case that the verses of threat concerning the disobedient are conditional upon not repenting, and even if this condition is not stated in the explicit text, they are conditional for us as well upon not being pardoned, even if this condition is not stated explicitly? Or we say: its meaning is that the sinner deserves these kinds of punishment, so the report about occurrence is taken as a report about deserving occurrence. This is the sum of what is said in establishing this doctrine.

As for those who affirmed the occurrence of punishment, they said: it has been transmitted to us by way of tawatur (mass transmission) from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that punishment occurs, so denying it would be denying the Messenger. As for the doubts you have relied upon in negating punishment, they are based on good and evil (husn and qubh), and that is something we do not hold to. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 2, verse 8 (part 1 of 2):

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers.﴾

Know that the exegetes unanimously agreed that this refers to the description of the hypocrites (munafiqun). They said: Allah described the three categories of people, the believers, the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and He began with the sincere believers whose inner states are sound and whose hearts are upright. Then He followed them with the disbelievers, whose characteristic is persistence in denial and obstinacy. Then He described the state of the one who says with his tongue that he is a believer while his heart contradicts that. On this there are several issues:

The first issue: Know that the discussion of the reality of hypocrisy cannot be clarified except through a division which we will mention.
