His teacher Abu Abd Allah al-Basri said: applying the name "creator" to God is impossible, because determination and leveling are expressions for thinking, reflection and calculation, and that is impossible with regard to God.

The majority of the People of the Sunnah and the Community said: creation is an expression for bringing into existence and originating. They argued for this with the statement of the Muslims: "There is no creator but God." And if creation were an expression for determination, that would not be valid.

* * *

**The third issue:** Know that He, glorified is He, commanded worship of Himself, and the command to worship Him depends on knowing that He exists. Since knowledge of His existence is not self-evident but acquired through reasoning, He has here mentioned what proves His existence.

Know also that we have explained in *al-Kutub al-'Aqliyya* ("the rational books") that the ways of establishing the existence of Allah, exalted is He, are either contingency (*imkan*), or origination in time (*huduth*), or both. Each of these is either in substances (*jawahir*) or in accidents (*a'rad*). Thus the total of the proofs indicating His existence, glorified and exalted is He, comes to six, with no more beyond them:

The first: reasoning from the contingency of essences. This is alluded to in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah is the Rich, and you are the poor﴾ [Muhammad: 38], in His words recounting Abraham: ﴿They are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 77], in His saying: ﴿And that to your Lord is the final end﴾ [al-Najm: 42], in His saying: ﴿Say, "Allah." Then leave them﴾ [al-An'am: 91], ﴿So flee to Allah﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 50], and ﴿Verily, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest﴾ [al-Ra'd: 28].

The second: reasoning from the contingency of attributes. This is alluded to in His saying: ﴿the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾, and in His saying: ﴿He who made the earth a bed for you and the sky a canopy﴾, as its explanation will come later.

The third: reasoning from the origination of bodies. This is alluded to in the saying of Abraham, peace be upon him: ﴿I do not love those that set﴾ [al-An'am: 76].

The fourth: reasoning from the origination of accidents. This method is the closest of the methods to the understanding of created beings, and it is confined to two matters:

[p. 90]

the evidences within the self (*dala'il al-anfus*) and the evidences in the horizons (*dala'il al-afaq*). The divine books mostly comprise these two categories, and Allah, exalted is He, has here combined these two aspects.

As for the evidences within the self: everyone knows by necessity that he did not exist before, that he now exists, and that whatever comes into being after non-existence must have a producer. That producer is neither the person himself, nor his parents, nor the rest of mankind, because the incapacity of created beings to produce such a composition is known by necessity. Therefore there must be a producer who differs from these existing things, so that it is valid for Him to bring these individuals into existence. However, one may object here: why should it not be possible that the producer is the natures of the seasons, the spheres, and the stars? Since this question is plausible, Allah, exalted is He, following it, mentioned what indicates that these things need an originator and producer, namely His saying: ﴿He who made the earth a bed for you and the sky a canopy﴾. This is what is meant by the evidences of the horizons, and it includes everything that occurs of changes in the conditions of the world: thunder, lightning, winds, clouds, and the alternation of the seasons. The summary of this comes down to this: celestial bodies and terrestrial bodies share corporeality, so the specialization of some of them with certain attributes, such as magnitudes, shapes, and places, cannot be due to corporeality itself or to any of its necessary properties. Otherwise, all of them would have to share those attributes. Therefore it must be due to a separate cause. If that cause is a body, the inquiry returns to why it was specifically endowed with that productive power among those bodies. If it is not a body, then it is either a necessitating agent or a choosing agent. The first is invalid, for otherwise the specialization of some bodies with some attributes would not be more appropriate than the reverse. So it must be a capable agent. Thus through this proof it is established that all bodies need a capable producer that is neither a body nor corporeal. At this point it becomes clear that reasoning from the origination of accidents to the existence of the Creator is not sufficient except after seeking help from the contingency of accidents and attributes.

Having understood this, we say: Allah, exalted is He, specifically placed this type of proof at the beginning of His Book for two reasons:

The first: since this method is the closest of the methods to the understanding of created beings and the most adhering to minds, and since the proofs mentioned in the Qur'an must be the furthest from subtlety and the nearest to understanding, so that everyone, from the elite and the common folk, may benefit from them, Allah, exalted is He, therefore mentioned that at the beginning of His Book.

The second: the purpose of the Qur'anic proofs is not disputation. Rather, their purpose is to establish true beliefs in the hearts. This type of proof is stronger than other methods in this domain, because this type of proof, just as it yields knowledge of the existence of the Creator, also reminds of the Creator's blessings upon us. Existence and life are great blessings upon us, and reminding of blessings brings about love, abandonment of contention, and the achievement of submission. For this reason, mentioning this type of proof is better than other types.

Know that the early generations (*al-salaf*) had subtle methods in this domain:

First: It is narrated that some of the *zanadiqa* (heretics) denied the Creator in the presence of Ja'far al-Sadiq, may Allah be pleased with him. Ja'far said: "Have you boarded the sea?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Have you seen its terrors?" He said: "Indeed. Once violent winds raged, breaking the ships and drowning the sailors. I clung to one of its planks, but then that plank slipped away from me, and I was tossed about in the crashing waves until I was thrown onto the shore." Ja'far said: "Your reliance was previously on the ship and the sailor, then on the plank, so that they might save you. When these things were gone from you, did you commit yourself to destruction, or were you still hoping for safety?" He said: "Rather, I hoped for safety." He said: "From whom were you hoping for it?" The man fell silent. Ja'far said: "The Creator is the One you were hoping in at that time, and He is the One who saved you from drowning." So the man embraced Islam at his hand.

Second: It is mentioned in the book *Diyanat al-'Arab* (*The Religions of the Arabs*) that the Prophet ﷺ said to 'Imran ibn Husayn: "How many gods do you have?" He said: "Seven: six on earth and one in heaven." He said: "Who among them do you rely on for your need, distress, and averting of great matters when they descend upon you?" He said: "Allah." He said, peace be upon him: "You have no god except Allah."

Third: Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, was a sword against the *Dahriyya* (materialists who denied a Creator), and they used to seize the opportunity to kill him. One day, while he was sitting in his mosque, a group rushed upon him with drawn swords and intended to kill him. He said to them: "Answer me a question, then do what you wish." They said: "Go on." He said: "What do you say about a man who tells you: 'I saw a ship loaded with cargo and filled with heavy goods, surrounded in the depths of the sea by crashing waves and varying winds, yet it was moving steadily, with no sailor to steer it and no keeper to guide it. Is that possible according to reason?'" They said: "No, this is something reason does not accept." Abu Hanifa said: "Glory be to Allah! If a ship sailing steadily in the sea without a keeper or a steersman is not possible according to reason, then how is it possible for this world to subsist with its varied conditions, its changing actions, the vastness of its expanses, and the diversity of its sides, without a Creator and a Guardian?" They all wept and said: "You have spoken the truth," and they sheathed their swords and repented.

Fourth: They asked al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, "What is the proof for the existence of the Creator?" He said: "The leaf of the mulberry: its taste, color, smell, and nature are one according to you?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then the silkworm eats it and silk emerges from it; the bee eats it and honey emerges from it; the sheep eats it and dung emerges from it; and the gazelles eat it and musk is formed in their musk pods. Who made these things differ in this way when the nature is one?" They admired his answer, embraced Islam at his hand, and they numbered seventeen.

Fifth: Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked another time, and he relied on the fact that the father desires a male but it becomes a female, and vice versa, and thereby he indicated the Creator.

Sixth: Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah be pleased with him, relied on a fortified, smooth fortress with no opening, its exterior like molten silver and its interior like pure gold. Then the walls split and there came forth from the fortress a living creature that hears and sees. There must be a doer. By "the fortress" he meant the egg, and by "the living creature" he meant the chick.

Seventh: Harun al-Rashid asked Malik about this, and he argued from the difference of voices, the repetition of melodies, and the variation of languages.

Eighth: Abu Nuwas was asked about it, and he said:

*Reflect on the vegetation of the earth, and look at the traces of what the King has made.*
*Eyes of silver, staring upward, and flowers like pure gold.*
*On stems of emerald, bearing witness that Allah has no partner.*

Ninth: A Bedouin was asked about the proof, and he said: "A dropping indicates a camel, dung indicates donkeys, and footprints indicate a path. So a sky with constellations, an earth with roads, and seas with waves: do they not indicate the Creator, the Forbearing, the Knowing, the Powerful?"

Tenth: A physician was asked: "How did you know your Lord?" He said: "By a dried myrobalan that releases, and a soothing saliva that retains." Another said: "I knew Him by a bee: one of its two ends produces honey, and the other stings; and honey is the reverse of a sting."

Eleventh: The judgment of intuition regarding His saying: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah"﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 87], and ﴿Then when they saw Our punishment, they said, "We believe in Allah alone, and we reject what we used to associate with Him"﴾ [Ghafir: 84].

\* \* \*

**The fourth issue:** The Qadi said: The benefit of His saying ﴿who created you﴾ is that worship is not deserved except by this. When He obligated His servants to worship, He explained what He has and because of which worship is obligatory. If it is asked: what is the benefit of His saying ﴿and those before you﴾, when the creation of those before them does not require worship from them? We answer: the answer is in two respects. The first: although the matter is as you have said, their knowledge that Allah, exalted is He, created them is like their knowledge that He created those before them, since the way of knowing this is one.

The second: those before them are like the roots for them, and the creation of roots operates in the manner of a favor upon the branches. So it is as if He, exalted is He, is reminding them of His great favor upon them, as if He is saying: Do not think that I bestowed favor upon you only when you came into being. Rather, I was bestowing favor upon you a thousand years before you came into being, because I was creating your roots and your fathers.

\* \* \*

**The fifth issue:** Concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿so that you may become righteous﴾ there are two discussions.

**The first discussion:** The word *la'alla* ("perhaps," "so that") expresses hope and apprehension. You say: *la'alla Zaydan yukrimuni* ("perhaps Zayd will honor me"). Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Perhaps he will remember or fear﴾ [Ta-Ha: 44], ﴿Perhaps the Hour is near﴾ [al-Shura: 17]. Do you not see His saying: ﴿Those who believe are apprehensive of it﴾ [al-Shura: 18]? Hope and apprehension arise only in the presence of ignorance of the outcome, and that is impossible for Allah, exalted is He. Therefore there must be an interpretation of it, and it comes in several ways:

The first: the meaning of *la'alla* refers to the servants and not to Allah, exalted is He. So His saying ﴿Perhaps he will remember or fear﴾ [Ta-Ha: 44] means: "Go, you two, upon your hope and expectation of his faith, though Allah, exalted is He, knows what his affair will come to."

The second: it is the custom of kings and great men that in their promises, which they prepare themselves to fulfill, they limit themselves to saying "perhaps," "maybe," and similar words, or they hint at the attainment of a glance, a smile, or a sweet look from them. When something of that sort is found, the seeker has no doubt of attaining what he sought. In this manner the word *la'alla* came in the speech of Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 2, verse 21 (part 7 of 7):

Third: it has been said that (لَعَلَّ, *la'alla*) means (كَيْ, *kay*, "so that"). The author of *al-Kashshaf* said: (لَعَلَّ) does not mean (كَيْ), but the word (لَعَلَّ) expresses hope and expectation. When the Generous, the Merciful, gives hope, He will certainly grant what is hoped for, so His expectations take the place of His binding promise. For this reason it has been said that (لَعَلَّ) in the speech of God Most High means (كَيْ). Fourth: God Most High has done for the responsible persons (mukallafun) what, if another had done it, would have given rise to hope that the intended aim would be achieved. For when God gave them the ability to choose good and evil, created for them guiding intellects, and removed their excuses, then anyone who does this for another hopes from him that the aim will be achieved. So the meaning of the word (لَعَلَّ) is the doing of what, if another had done it, would have made hope necessary. Fifth: al-Qaffal said: (لَعَلَّ) is derived from the repetition of a thing, like their saying: "*'alalan ba'da nahalin*" (repeated drinking after drinking). Its (ل) is the (ل) of emphasis, like the (ل) that enters (لَقَدْ). So the origin of (لَعَلَّ) is (عَلَّ), because they say: (عَلَّكَ أنْ تَفْعَلَ كَذا), meaning (لَعَلَّكَ). When its essence is repetition and emphasis, the saying of someone: "Do such-and-such, perhaps you will attain your need," means: do it, for your doing it strengthens your request and empowers you to it.

The second point of discussion: One may say that if worship is taqwa, then His saying: "Worship your Lord, so that you may have taqwa" is like saying: "Worship your Lord, so that you may worship," or: "Fear your Lord, so that you may fear." The answer has two aspects. The first:

We do not grant that worship is itself taqwa. Rather, worship is an act through which taqwa is attained, because (الِاتِّقاء, *al-ittiqa'*) is guarding oneself against harms, while worship is the performance of what is commanded. The very act is not the same as guarding oneself against harms, but it necessitates such guarding. So it is as if God Most High said: "Worship your Lord so that you may guard yourselves by it against His punishment." And when it is said of the act itself that it is (اتِّقاء), that is a metaphor, because (الِاتِّقاء) is other than that by which (الِاتِّقاء) is attained. But because one of the two is connected to the other, the name of the one is applied to the other. The second: God Most High created the responsible persons only so that they would have taqwa and obey, as He said: "I did not create the jinn and humankind except that they should worship Me" (Surah al-Dhariyat 51:56). So it is as if God Most High commanded the worship of the Lord who created them for this purpose. This interpretation suits the principles of the Mu'tazila (al-Mu'tazilah).

* * *

The sixth issue: Abu 'Amr read (خَلَقكُّمْ, *khalaqakkum*) with idgham (assimilation of the two consonants). Abu al-Sammaifa' read (وخَلَقَ مَن قَبْلَكُمْ, "and He created those before you"), and Zayd ibn 'Ali read (والَّذِينَ مَن قَبْلَكم, "and those who were before you"). The author of *al-Kashshaf* said: The explanation of this is that he inserted the second relative pronoun (الموصول) between the first one and its complement (صلة) for emphasis, just as Jarir inserted the second (تيما) between the first and what was added to it in his saying:

"O Taym of Taym 'Adi, may you have no father,
Taym the second, between the first and what is attached to it."

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 2, verse 22 (part 1 of 5):**

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Who made the earth a bed for you, and the sky a canopy, and sent down water from the sky, and brought forth with it fruits as provision for you. So do not set up rivals to God while you know [that He alone is your Lord]﴾. Concerning it there are several issues:

**The first issue:** The word (alladhi, "who"), together with its relative clause (sila), is either in the accusative position as a qualifying description of (alladhi khalaqakum, "who created you"), or it is used for praise and glorification. Or it may be in the nominative position as the subject of a nominal sentence (mubtada'), in which case it carries the same praise that the accusative carries.

**The second issue:** (alladhi) is a word put to indicate a single referent when one tries to define it by a known proposition (qadiyya ma'lumah). For example, you say: "The man whose father is departing has left." "His father is departing" is a known proposition. When you want to define the man by this known proposition, you introduce (alladhi) to him. This is the verification of their saying that it is used to describe definite nouns (ma'arif) by clauses (jumal). Once this is established, His saying: ﴿Who made the earth a bed for you and the sky a canopy﴾ implies that they were aware of the existence of something that made the earth a bed and the sky a canopy. This is the confirmation of His saying: ﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say, "God."﴾ [Luqman: 25].

**The third issue:** God, Exalted is He, mentioned here five kinds of proofs: two from the self (anfus) and three from the horizons (afaq). He began first with His saying: ﴿created you﴾; second, with the fathers and mothers, which is His saying: ﴿and those before you﴾; third, with the earth being a bed; fourth, with the sky being a canopy; and fifth, with the matters resulting from the combination of sky and earth, which is His saying: ﴿and sent down water from the sky and brought forth with it fruits as provision for you﴾.

There are reasons for this order. The first is that the thing closest to a human being is himself, and a person's knowledge of his own condition is more evident than his knowledge of the conditions of others. Since the purpose of reasoning (istidlal) is to convey knowledge, whatever is more evident in indication is stronger in conveying knowledge and more deserving of mention. For this reason He mentioned the human self first, then paired it with the fathers and mothers, then made the earth the third. This is because the earth is closer to a human being than the sky, and a human knows the condition of the earth better than the conditions of the sky. He mentioned the sky before the descent of water from it and the emergence of fruits by its means, because that is like a matter produced from the sky and the earth, and the effect comes after the cause. For this reason God delayed its mention after the mention of the earth and the sky.

The second reason is that the creation of responsible beings (mukallafun) as living, capable beings is the root of all blessings, whereas the creation of the earth, the sky and the water is benefited from only on condition that creation, life, power and desire exist. Therefore He rightly mentioned the roots before the branches.

[Page 94]

The third reason is that everything in the earth and the sky that is a sign of the Creator is present in the human being, and there are in the human being signs that are not present in those two. A human has life, power, desire and intellect, and none of these can be produced by anyone except God, Exalted is He. Since the aspects of proof for Him here are more complete, it was more deserving to put them first. Know that, just as we have mentioned the reason for the order, we should also mention the benefits in each of these three.

\* \* \*

**The fourth issue:** Know that He, glorified and exalted, mentioned here that He made the earth a bed. A similar expression is His saying: ﴿Or who made the earth a resting place and made rivers through it?﴾ [al-Naml: 61], and His saying: ﴿Who made the earth for you a cradle﴾ [Ta-Ha: 53; al-Zukhruf: 10]. Know that the earth being a bed is conditioned on several matters:

**The first condition:** that it be still. For if it were moving, its motion would either be in a straight line or in a circular motion. If its motion were in a straight line, it would not be a bed for us at all, because whoever leaps from a high place must not reach the ground, since the earth is falling and the human is falling, and the earth is heavier than the human. When two heavy bodies fall, the heavier of them is faster, and the slower does not catch up with the faster. So the human ought not to reach the earth. Thus it is established that if it were falling, it would not be a bed.

As for if its motion were circular, our benefit from it would not be complete. For example, if the earth's motion were toward the east, and a person wanted to move toward the west, there is no doubt that the earth's motion would be faster. Then the person would have to remain in his place and be unable to reach where he wants. But since that is possible for him, we know that the earth is not moving, neither circularly nor in a straight line. So it is still.

Then they differed about the cause of this stillness in several ways:

The first: the earth has no limit on the lower side, and if that is so, it has no place to descend to, so it does not fall. This is corrupt, because it has been established by proof that bodies are finite.

The second: those who accepted that bodies are finite said: the earth is not a sphere but is like half a sphere, its convex part is upward and its flat surface is downward, and that flat surface is placed upon water and air. It is in the nature of a heavy thing, when it is spread out, to flatten upon water and air, like a lead plate: when it is spread out it floats on water, and if it is gathered it sinks. This is false for two reasons. First: the inquiry into the cause of water and air standing is like the inquiry into the cause of the earth standing. Second: why did that side of the earth become spread out until it rested on water, while this side became convex?

The third: those who said that the cause of the earth's stillness is the pull of the celestial sphere (falak) on it from all sides, so its being pulled toward some sides was no more deserving than others, and so it remained in the middle. This is false for two reasons. First: the smaller is quicker to be pulled than the larger, so why is the particle not pulled toward the sphere? Second: the nearer is more deserving of being pulled, so a particle thrown upward is more deserving of being pulled, and it ought not to return.

The fourth: the view of those who made the cause of its stillness the pushing of the celestial sphere on it from all sides, like when a bit of dust is placed in a bottle and the bottle is spun rapidly on its axis: the dust stands in the middle of the bottle because the push is equal from all sides. This too is false for five reasons:

First: if the push reached this degree of strength, why does none of us feel it?

Second: why does this push not make the movement of clouds and winds go in one specific direction?

Third: why did it not make their movement toward the west easier than their movement toward the east?

Fourth: it must be that the heavier a body is, the slower its motion, because the movement of the larger body from a compelling pusher is slower than the movement of the smaller.

Fifth: the motion of a heavy falling body at the start must be faster than its motion at the end, because at the start it is farther from the sphere.

The fifth: that the earth by nature seeks the center of the sphere. This is the saying of Aristotle (Arisṭāṭālīs) and the majority of his followers. This too is weak, because bodies are equal in corporeality, so the specification of some of them by the attribute for which they seek that state must be possible, and therefore requires a choosing agent.

The sixth: Abu Hashim said: the lower half of the earth contains upward tendencies (i'timadat), and the upper half contains downward tendencies, so the two tendencies push against each other and so stillness follows. The objection to this is that the specification of each of the two halves with a particular attribute is not possible except by a choosing agent.

From what we have mentioned, it is established that the stillness of the earth is nothing but from God, Exalted is He.

At this point we say: look at the earth and you will know that it is stable without any suspension above it or any support beneath it. As for there being no suspension above it, this is evident. Moreover, if it were suspended by a suspender, the suspender would need another suspender, without end. By this reasoning it is established that there is no support beneath it, so we know there must be something that holds it by His power and choice. For this reason God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease; and if they should cease, none could hold them after Him﴾ [Fatir: 41].

**The second condition** for the earth being a bed for us: that it not be extremely hard like stone, for sleeping and walking on it would then cause pain to the body. Also, if the earth were made of gold, for example, cultivation on it would be impossible, and buildings could not be made from it, because digging and assembling it as desired would be impossible. Nor should it be extremely soft, like water into which the foot sinks.

**The third condition:** that it not be extremely fine and transparent. For a transparent thing does not hold light upon it, and whatever is like that does not warm from the stars and the sun, so it would become very cold. God therefore made it dusty so that light would rest upon it and it would warm, and thus be suitable to be a bed for animals.

**The fourth condition:** that it be exposed above the water. For the nature of the earth is to be submerged in water, and so the seas would have to surround the earth. If that were so, it would not be a bed for us. So God reversed the nature of the earth and brought some of its sides out of the water, like an exposed island, until it became suitable to be a bed for us.

Some people claimed that the condition for the earth to be a bed is that it not be a sphere, and they used this verse to show that the earth is not a sphere. This is very far-fetched, because when a sphere is very large, a piece of it is like a flat surface in its capacity to be stood upon. What further confirms this is that the mountains are the pegs of the earth, and then standing upon them is possible. So this view is more appropriate. And God knows best.

\* \* \*

**The fifth issue:** concerning the remaining benefits and attributes of the earth:

The first benefit: the things generated in it, such as minerals, plants, animals, and the heavenly and earthly phenomena, none knows their details except God, Exalted is He.

The second: that moist things mix with it, so that cohesion occurs in the bodies of compounds.

The third: the variety of the earth's regions. Some of it is soft, some hard, some sandy, some saline, and some volcanic, ﹝Page 96﹞ as in His saying: ﴿And in the earth there are adjacent tracts﴾ [al-Ra'd: 4], and He said: ﴿And the good land—its vegetation comes forth by the permission of its Lord, and that which is corrupt yields only meager growth﴾ [al-A'raf: 58].

The fourth: the variety of its colors. Some is red, white, black, ash-colored and dust-colored, as He said: ﴿And among the mountains are streaks, white and red, of varying shades, and extremely black﴾ [Fatir: 27].

The fifth: its splitting open for vegetation. He said: ﴿By the earth that splits open﴾ [al-Tariq: 12].

The sixth: its being a storehouse for the water sent down from the sky, to which the indication is His saying: ﴿And We sent down water from the sky in measure, and We caused it to settle in the earth, and indeed, We are able to take it away﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 18], and His saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if your water should sink away, who could bring you flowing water?﴾ [al-Mulk: 30].

The seventh: the springs and great rivers in it, to which the indication is His saying: ﴿And He placed in it firm mountains and rivers﴾ [al-Ra'd: 3].

The eighth: the minerals and metals in it, to which the indication is His saying: ﴿And the earth—We spread it out, cast into it firm mountains, and caused to grow in it of every thing in balanced measure﴾ [al-Hijr: 19]. Then He explained the matter fully after that, saying: ﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasuries, and We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾ [al-Hijr: 21].

The ninth: the hidden (khab') that the earth brings forth from grain and date-stones. He said: ﴿Indeed, God splits the grain and the date-stone﴾ [al-An'am: 95], and He said: ﴿He brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Naml: 25].

Furthermore, the earth has the nature of generosity, for you give it one grain and it returns to you seven hundred: ﴿Like a grain that grows seven spikes, in each spike a hundred grains﴾ [al-Baqarah: 261].

**The tenth:** its life after its death. God the Exalted says: ﴿Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren land and bring forth thereby crops?﴾ [al-Sajdah 32:27], and He says: ﴿And a sign for them is the dead earth; We have brought it to life and brought forth from it grain, so from it they eat﴾ [Yasin 36:33].

**The eleventh:** the diverse colors, forms and kinds of creatures upon it. To this He alludes in His words: ﴿He created the heavens without pillars that you see, and cast into the earth firm mountains lest it shake with you, and dispersed therein every kind of moving creature﴾ [Luqman 31:10].

**The twelfth:** the plants upon it, with their diverse colors, kinds and benefits. To this He alludes in His words: ﴿And We caused to grow therein of every beautiful pair﴾ [Qaf 50:7]. The diversity of its colors is a sign, the diversity of its tastes is a sign, and the diversity of its scents is a sign. Some of it is the food of humans and some the food of animals, as He said: ﴿Eat and let your livestock graze﴾ [Taha 20:54]. As for human food, some of it is staple, some is condiment, some is medicine, some is fruit, and some are the various kinds differing in sweetness and sourness. God the Exalted said: ﴿And He determined therein its sustenance in four days, complete for those who ask﴾ [Fussilat 41:10]. Furthermore, some of it is human clothing, since clothing is either of plant origin, such as cotton and flax, or of animal origin, such as hair, wool, silk and hides, and these come from the animals that God the Exalted dispersed upon the earth. So the food is from the earth and the clothing is from the earth. Then He said: ﴿and He creates what you do not know﴾ [al-Nahl 16:8], and in this is an allusion to many benefits that none knows but God the Exalted.

Then, indeed, He the Glorified and Exalted made the earth a covering for your ugliness after your death, and He said: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle, for the living and the dead?﴾ [al-Mursalat 77:25–26]. ﴿From it We created you and into it We will return you﴾ [Taha 20:55]. Then, indeed, He the Glorified and Exalted combined these great benefits of the sky and the earth, and He said: ﴿and subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ [al-Jathiyah 45:13].

**The thirteenth:** the diverse stones upon it. Among the small ones are those suitable for adornment, so their gems are made into rings, and among the large ones are those used for buildings. Consider the stone from which fire comes out despite its abundance, and consider the red ruby despite its rarity. Then consider the great benefit gained from that lowly thing and the small benefit gained from this noble thing.

**The fourteenth:** what God the Exalted deposited in it of noble minerals, such as gold and silver. Then reflect: humans have extracted fine crafts and magnificent trades, they have brought fish up from the depths of the sea, and they have brought birds down from the heights of the air. Yet they have been unable to create gold and silver. The reason is that the only benefit in their existence is their value as currency, and this benefit is attained only when they are scarce. Whoever is able to create them would nullify this wisdom. Therefore God set up a closed door before them, to manifest this wisdom and to preserve this blessing. For this reason, whatever causes no harm to creation He has enabled them to obtain, so they are able to make imitation pieces from copper and glass from sand. When the intelligent person reflects upon these subtleties and wonders, he is compelled, by the need of these arrangements, to acknowledge a wise, powerful, knowing Maker, glorified and exalted is He above what the wrongdoers say, a great exaltation.

**The fifteenth:** the abundance, upon the mountains and lands, of trees suitable for building and for roofs, and then for firewood, and how great is the need for it in baking and cooking. God the Exalted has drawn attention to the signs and benefits of the earth in words that eloquent speakers cannot reach and that the articulate cannot match, when He said: ﴿And He it is who spread out the earth and placed therein firm mountains and rivers, and from all fruits He made therein two mates, two﴾ [al-Ra'd 13:3]. As for rivers, some are great, such as the Nile, the Seyhan, the Ceyhan and the Euphrates, and some are small, and they are many. All of them carry sweet water for irrigation, farming and all other benefits.

**The sixth issue:** whether the sky is superior or the earth.

Some said: the sky is superior, for several reasons:

First: the sky is the place of worship of the angels, and there is not a spot in it where anyone has disobeyed God.

Second: when Adam, peace be upon him, committed that disobedience in the Garden, it was said to him: "Descend from the Garden," and God the Exalted said: "No one who disobeys Me shall dwell in My neighborhood."

Third: His words: ﴿And We made the sky a protected ceiling﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:32], and His words: ﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations﴾ [al-Furqan 25:61]; no such description was given of the earth.

Fourth: in most instances the mention of the sky precedes the earth in the text.

Others said: rather, the earth is superior, for several reasons:

"A": God the Exalted described certain parts of the earth as blessed, in His words: ﴿Indeed, the first House placed for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:96]; "B": ﴿in the blessed spot from the tree﴾ [al-Qasas 28:30]; "C": ﴿to the farthest mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed﴾ [al-Isra' 17:1]; "D": He described the land of Syria as blessed, saying: ﴿the eastern parts of the earth and its western parts, which We had blessed﴾ [al-A'raf 7:137].

Fifth: He described the whole earth as blessed, saying: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve...﴾ [Fussilat 41:9], up to His words: ﴿and He placed in it firm mountains from above it and blessed it﴾ [Fussilat 41:10]. If it is said: "What blessing is there in the desolate wastelands and deadly deserts?" We reply: they are dwellings and pasture for wild animals, and then they are dwellings for people when they need them. For these blessings God the Exalted said: ﴿And on the earth are signs for those of certainty﴾ [al-Dhariyat 51:20]. And although these signs are present for those who are not certain, since none benefits from them except the certain, He made them signs for the certain, honoring them,

\* \* \*

**[Page 98]**

just as He said: ﴿guidance for the righteous﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:2].

Sixth: God the Glorified and Exalted created the noble prophets from the earth, as He said: ﴿From it We created you and into it We will return you﴾ [Taha 20:55], and He did not create anything from the heavens, because He said: ﴿And We made the sky a protected ceiling﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:32].

Seventh: God the Exalted honored His Prophet by it, making the whole earth a place of prostration for him, and making its dust a means of purification.

\* \* \*

As for the statement (the sky as a structure), there are several issues:

**The first issue:** God the Exalted has mentioned the matter of the heavens and the earth in His Book in many places. There is no doubt that the frequent mention by God of the heavens and the earth indicates the greatness of their station, and that He, the Glorified and Exalted, has in them great secrets and profound wisdoms that human understanding and intellects do not reach.

**The second issue:** on the virtues of the sky. These are of several aspects:

The first: God the Exalted adorned it with seven things: with the lamps, ﴿And We have certainly adorned the nearest heaven with lamps﴾ [al-Mulk 67:5]; with the moon, ﴿and made the moon therein a light﴾ [Nuh 71:16]; with the sun, ﴿and made the sun a lamp﴾ [Nuh 71:16]; with the Throne, ﴿Lord of the Mighty Throne﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:129]; with the Kursi (the Footstool), ﴿His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:255]; with the Preserved Tablet, ﴿in a preserved tablet﴾ [al-Buruj 85:22]; and with the Pen, ﴿Nun. By the pen﴾ [al-Qalam 68:1]. These are seven: three of them are apparent, and four are hidden, established by the textual proofs from verses and reports.

The second: God the Exalted named the heavens with names that indicate the greatness of their station: sky, a protected ceiling, seven layers, and seven strong ones. Then He mentioned the outcome of their affair, saying: ﴿And when the sky is split open﴾ [al-Mursalat 77:9]; ﴿And when the sky is stripped away﴾ [al-Takwir 81:11]; ﴿the Day We will fold up the sky﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:104]; ﴿the Day the sky will be like murky oil﴾ [al-Ma'arij 70:8]; ﴿the Day the sky will shake violently﴾ [al-Tur 52:9]; ﴿and it will be rose-colored like oil﴾ [al-Rahman 55:37]. He mentioned its beginning in two verses, saying: ﴿Then He turned to the sky while it was smoke﴾ [Fussilat 41:11], and He said: ﴿Have those who disbelieved not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass and We separated them?﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:30]. This intense detailing of how they came into being and how they will perish indicates that He, the Glorified, created them for a profound wisdom, as He said: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieved﴾ [Sad 38:27].

The third: God the Exalted made the sky the direction of supplication. Hands are raised toward it, and faces turn toward it. It is the abode of lights, the place of clarity, illumination, purity, and protection from defect and corruption.

The fourth: some said: the heavens and the earths have two attributes. The heavens act without being acted upon, while the earths are acted upon without acting. The agent is more noble than the recipient, and for this reason the mention of the sky is mostly placed before the earth. Also, in most instances the heavens are mentioned in the plural and the earth in the singular, because there must be many heavens so that through them the various conjunctions of the planets and the changing of the places of the rays may occur, whereas the earth is receptive, so one earth was sufficient.

The fifth: reflect upon the color of the sky and the wise arrangement in it. This color is the most agreeable of colors to the eye and the most strengthening to it, so much so that physicians order whoever has eye pain to look at blue. Consider how God the Exalted made the surface of the sky colored with this blue color so that the seeing eyes that look upon it may benefit from it. He, the Glorified and Exalted, made its color the most beneficial of colors, which is the luminous, and its shape the best of shapes, which is the round. For this reason He said: ﴿Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We constructed it and adorned it, and there are no gaps in it?﴾ [Qaf 50:6], meaning: no fissures in it. Had it been a ceiling not enclosing the earth, there would have been gaps.

\* \* \*

**The third issue:** on explaining the virtues of the sky and the virtues of what is in it, namely the sun, the moon and the stars.

As for the sun, reflect upon its rising and its setting. Were it not for that, the whole world's affairs would collapse, and how would people strive for their livelihoods? The benefit of its rising is evident, but consider the benefit of its setting. Were it not for its setting, people would have no quiet or rest, though they need quiet and rest to attain comfort, to activate the digestive power, and to carry nourishment to the limbs, as God the Exalted said: ﴿He it is who made the night for you to rest therein and the day giving sight﴾ [Yunus 10:67]. Also, were it not for setting, greed would drive people to persist in work, as He said: ﴿And We made the night a covering, and We made the day for livelihood﴾ [al-Naba' 78:10–11]. Third: were it not for setting, the earth would be heated by the sun's rising upon it until every animal upon it burned and every plant upon it perished, as He said: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord extends the shadow? Had He willed, He would have made it stationary﴾ [al-Furqan 25:45]. Thus, by the wisdom of the Truth, the Glorified and Exalted, the sun rises at one time and sets at another, like a lamp given to a household according to their need and then removed from them so that they may settle and rest. Thus light and darkness, though opposed to each other, become cooperating and mutually supporting in what brings about the good of the world. All of this concerns the rising and setting of the sun.

As for the sun's rising and descent, God the Exalted made it a cause for the establishment of the four seasons. In winter, the heat recedes into the trees and plants, so the substances of fruits are generated from it, the air becomes gentle, and clouds and rain increase. The bodies of animals become stronger because the innate heat (al-ḥarāra al-gharīziyya, the natural vital warmth of the body) is retained within. In spring, the natures stir and the substances generated in winter emerge, so plants sprout, trees blossom, and animals become excited for mating. In summer, the air grows hot, so fruits ripen, the superfluities of bodies are dissolved, the surface of the earth dries, and it becomes ready for building and construction. In autumn, dryness and cold appear, so bodies gradually move toward winter, for if the transition occurred all at once, bodies would perish and decay.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 2, verse 22 (part 3 of 5):

As for the movement of the sun, then consider its benefits. If it were stationary in one place, the heat would intensify in that place and the cold would intensify in all other places. But it rises at the beginning of the day from the east, so it falls upon what lies opposite it in the west. Then it never ceases to revolve, covering one direction after another, until it reaches sunset, and then it shines upon the eastern regions. Thus no uncovered place remains without taking a share of the sun's rays. Also, it is as if God, exalted is He, were saying: If it stood on the eastern side, while the rich man had raised his building over the poor man's window, the light would not reach the poor man. But He, exalted is He, says: If the rich man has blocked the sun's light from him, then I will turn the sphere and turn the sun around him until the poor man takes his share.

As for the benefits of its inclination in its movement away from the line of equinox, we say: If the stars had no movement in inclination, the influence would be restricted to a single spot. The other regions would be empty of the benefits that come from it, and whatever lay near it would have uniform conditions, and the force there would be of one quality. If it were hot, it would consume the moistures and turn them all into fire, and the generated things would not come into being. So the place opposite the path of the stars would have one quality, the line that does not face it would have another quality, and a line between them would have an intermediate quality. Thus in one place there would be perpetual winter, in which there is wind and dust; in another place perpetual summer, which causes burning; and in another place spring or autumn in which ripening does not complete. And if there were no successive returns, and the stars moved slowly, the inclination would be of little benefit and the influence would be excessively intense, and what had no inclination would come about nearly. And if the stars moved faster than this, the benefits would not be perfected or completed. But when there is an inclination that keeps the movement in one direction for a period, and then it shifts to another direction as much as needed, and it remains in each direction for a while of time, its influence is thereby completed and its benefit is multiplied. Glory be to the Creator, the Manager with perfect wisdom and infinite power.

This is about the moon, which is called the sign of the night. Know that He, glory be to Him and exalted is He, made its rising and its setting beneficial. He made its rising beneficial at one time and its setting beneficial at another time. As for its setting, there is benefit in it for one who flees from his enemy, for the night covers him and hides him, so no pursuer reaches him and he escapes. Were it not for the darkness, the enemy would overtake him. This is what is meant by the words of al-Mutanabbi:

"How many a favor I have from the darkness of night, which proves that the Manichaeans are liars."

As for its rising, there is benefit in it for one who has lost something that the darkness hid and the moon revealed. There is a story: a Bedouin slept one night and lost his camel. When the moon rose, he found it. He looked at the moon and said: "God has fashioned you and illuminated you, and has made you revolve over the constellations. When He wills, He illuminates you, and when He wills, He folds you up. I know of no addition I can ask of Him for you. If you have given me joy, God has given you light." Then he recited:

"What shall I say, when my speech about you is brief, and you have spared me detail and summary?
If I say, 'May you never cease to be exalted,' you are such; or if I say, 'My Lord has adorned you,' He has indeed done so."

Among the Arabs there were those who disparaged the moon and said: "The moon brings the appointed time near, exposes the thief, overtakes the fugitive, exposes the lover, wears out linen, makes young men old, makes one forget the memory of loved ones, brings debts near, and draws near the calamity."

There were also among them those who preferred the moon over the sun for several reasons:

The first: the moon is masculine and the sun is feminine. But al-Mutanabbi criticized this with his words:

"The femininity of the name of the sun is no defect, nor is the masculinity a glory for the crescent."

The second: they said "the two moons" (al-qamarān), making the sun a follower of the moon.

Others preferred the sun over the moon because God, exalted is He, mentioned it before the moon in His saying: ﴿The sun and the moon by a reckoning﴾ [al-Rahman: 5], and ﴿By the sun and its brightness, and by the moon when it follows it﴾ [al-Shams: 1–2]. However, this argument is refuted by His saying: ﴿Among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾ [al-Taghabun: 2]; and He said: ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal﴾ [al-Hashr: 20]; and He said: ﴿He created death and life﴾ [al-Mulk: 2]; and He said: ﴿Indeed, with hardship comes ease﴾ [al-Sharh: 6]; and He said: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾ [Fatir: 32], and so on.

As for the stars, there are benefits in them:

The first benefit: that they are missiles against the devils. The second: knowing the qibla by them. The third: that the traveler may be guided by them on land and sea. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And it is He who placed for you the stars that you may be guided by them in the darknesses of land and sea﴾ [al-An'am: 97].

Then the stars are of three categories: those that set and do not rise, like the southern constellations; those that rise and do not set, like the northern ones; and some of them set at times and rise at other times. Also, some of them are fixed stars, some are wandering planets, some are eastern and some are western. The discussion of these is lengthy. As for what the philosophers claim regarding knowledge of the bodies and their distances:

[p. 101]

"Leave aside a sea in which the swimmers have drowned."

God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Knower of the unseen; He does not disclose His unseen to anyone, except to a messenger whom He has approved﴾ [al-Jinn: 26–27]; and He said: ﴿And you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾ [al-Isra': 85]; and He said: ﴿And I do not say to you that I have the treasures of God, nor do I know the unseen﴾ [Hud: 31]; and He said: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves﴾ [al-Kahf: 51]. Creation has failed to know their own essences and attributes, so how can they know the most distant things from them? The Arabs, despite their distance from knowing realities, knew this. One of them said:

"I know what is in today and yesterday before it, but regarding the knowledge of what is in tomorrow, I am blind."

Labid said:

"By God, the diviners with pebbles do not know, nor do the bird-augurs, what God is doing."

* * *

The fourth issue: on explaining that the sky is a building. Al-Jahiz said: When you reflect on this world, you find it like a house prepared with everything one needs. The sky is raised like a roof, the earth is spread out like a carpet, the stars shine like lamps, man is like the owner of the house who disposes of it, the kinds of plants are prepared for his benefits, and the kinds of animals are subjected to serve his interests. This is a clear summary indicating that the world was created with perfect management, comprehensive measure, consummate wisdom, and infinite power. And God knows best.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He sent down from the sky water, and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you﴾, know that when God created the earth, and it was like the oyster-shell containing the pearl, in which Adam and his offspring were deposited, then God knew the types of their needs. It is as if He said: "O Adam, I will not make you need anything other than this earth, which is for you like a mother." So He said: ﴿Indeed, We poured down water in torrents; then We split the earth in splitting﴾ [Abasa: 25–26]. Look, O My servant: the most precious things with you are gold and silver. If I had created the earth from gold and silver, would these benefits come from it? Then I placed these things in this world, although it is a prison; so what is the state in Paradise? The conclusion is that the earth is your mother, rather more compassionate than a mother, because a mother gives you one kind of milk, while the earth feeds you with various kinds of food. Then He said: ﴿From it We created you, and into it We will return you﴾ [Ta-Ha: 55]. Its meaning is: We will return you to this mother. This is not a threat, for a person is not threatened with his mother. That is because your place in the mother who bore you is narrower than your place in the earth. Moreover, you were in your mother's womb for nine months, and hunger and thirst did not touch you; so how will it be when you enter the greater mother's womb? But the condition is that you enter the womb of this greater mother just as you were in the womb of the lesser mother, for when you were in the womb of the lesser mother you had no fault, let alone a great sin. Rather, you were obedient to God, such that once He called you to come out into the world, you came out head first, in obedience to your Lord. Today He calls you seventy times to prayer, and you do not respond to Him with your feet.

Know that when He, glory be to Him and exalted is He, mentioned the earth and the sky, He explained the relation between them, a semblance of the marriage contract, through the descent of water from the sky onto the earth, and the bringing forth from its womb of things resembling the offspring produced by animals, and of kinds of fruits as provision, so that they would reflect upon themselves, and upon the states of what is above them and below them, and know that none of these things can bring about its creation and fashioning except One who differs from them in essence and attributes. That is the Wise Creator, glory be to Him and exalted is He.

Here there are questions:

[p. 102]

The first question: Do you say that God, exalted is He, is the Creator of these fruits as a consequence of water reaching them by the customary course, or do you say that God, exalted is He, created in the water a potent nature, and in the earth a receptive nature, so that when they combine, the effect arises from that power which God, exalted is He, created?

The answer: Without doubt, in both views there must be a Wise Creator.

As for the detail, we say: Without doubt, He, exalted is He, is able to create these fruits from the outset without these intermediaries, because the fruit has no meaning except a body in which exist taste, color, fragrance, and moisture. The body is receptive to these attributes, and these attributes are within God's power from the outset; for what makes them capable of being power-subject is either createdness (huduth), or possibility (imkan), or both. In any of these cases, it follows that God, exalted is He, is able to create these accidents in the body from the outset without these intermediaries. What strengthens this rational proof among the transmitted proofs is the report that He, exalted is He, brings into being the bliss of the people of Paradise for those who are rewarded, without these intermediaries. However, we say: His power to create them from the outset does not negate His power over them through the means of creating these influencing and receptive powers in bodies. The apparent view of the later theologians is the denial of this, and a proof is necessary for it.

The second question: Since He is able to create these fruits without these intermediaries, what is the wisdom in creating them through these intermediaries over this long period?

The answer: God does what He wills and decrees what He desires.

Then they mentioned several detailed wisdoms:

The first: God, exalted is He, has established the custom that He does not do this except in order and gradually. For when the responsible ones bear hardship in plowing and planting, seeking fruits, and exert themselves in this step by step, they know that since they need to bear these hardships to seek these worldly benefits, then it is more appropriate that they bear lesser hardships to seek the otherworldly benefits, which are greater than the worldly benefits. This is like what we said: He, exalted is He, is able to create healing without taking medicine, but He has established His custom of making it dependent upon it. For when one bears the bitterness of medicines to repel the harm of illness, then it is more appropriate that he bear the burdens of obligation to repel the harm of punishment.

The second: if He had created them at once without these intermediaries, the necessary knowledge would have arisen that they are ascribed to the Powerful, the Wise. That would be almost incompatible with obligation and trial. But if He created them through these intermediaries, then the responsible one, in ascribing them to the Powerful, would need careful reflection and subtle thought, and thus would merit reward. For this reason it is said: "Were it not for causes, no doubter would doubt."

The third: that there may perhaps be lessons in that for the angels and for those who seek insight, and correct reflections.

**Question 3:** His saying, ﴿and sent down water from the sky﴾, implies that rain descends from the sky. But this is not the case. Rain is actually formed from vapours that rise from the earth and ascend to the cold layer of the air, where they gather because of the cold. After they gather, they fall, and that is the rain.

The answer has several aspects:

First, the sky (*samā'*) is so called because of its loftiness (*sumuww*). Whatever is above you is a *samā'*. So when something descends from the clouds, it has descended from the sky.

Second, the thing that stirs those moist particles from the depths of the earth is the moist particles themselves, ﴿and sent down water from the sky﴾.

Third, God's word is the truth, and He has informed us that He sends down rain from the sky. When we know that it also descends from the clouds, it must be said that it descends from the sky to the clouds and from the clouds to the earth.

**Question 4:** What is the meaning of "min" (from) in His saying, ﴿from the fruits﴾?

The answer has two possibilities:

One is that it indicates partiality (*tab'īḍ*), because the two indefinite nouns, namely *mā'an* (water) and *rizqan* (provision), are adjacent to it, and their indefiniteness is intended to convey the meaning of partiality. It is as if it were said: "We sent down from the sky some of the water, and by it We brought forth some of the fruits as some of your provision."

The second is that it is explanatory (*bayān*), as in your saying, "I spent from the dirhams," meaning spending.

If it is asked, "On what is *rizqan* in the accusative?" We say: if *min* is partitive, then its accusative is because it is an object of purpose (*maf'ūl lahu*). If it is explanatory, then it is the object of *akhraja* (He brought forth).

**Question 5:** The fruit brought forth by the water of the sky is abundant, so why is it said *al-thamarāt* (the fruits) rather than *al-thamar* or *al-thimār*?

The answer: as an alert to the scarcity of the fruits of this world, and as an indication of the magnitude of the matter of the Hereafter. And God knows best.

As for His saying, ﴿So do not set up rivals to God while you know﴾, there are several questions.

**Question 1:** To what does His saying ﴿So do not set up﴾ relate?

The answer has three aspects:

First, that it relates to the command, meaning: worship, so do not set up rivals to God, for the origin and foundation of worship is monotheism (*tawḥīd*).

Second, that it relates to *la'alla* (so that), and the meaning is: He created you so that you may be God-fearing and fear His punishment, so do not ascribe to Him a rival, for it is one of the greatest causes of punishment.

Third, that it relates to His saying, ﴿Who made for you the earth a bed﴾, meaning: He is the One who created these dazzling signs for you, so do not take for Him partners.

**Question 2:** What is *nidd* (rival)? The answer: it is the equal that contends (*al-mithl al-munāzi'*). *Nāddattu al-rajul* means I opposed the man, from *nadda nudūdan*, when he fled or was contrary; it is as if each of the two rivals opposes his companion, that is, contends with him and sets himself against him.

If it is said: They did not say that the idols contend with God. We say: when they worshipped them and called them gods, their state resembled the state of one who believes that they are gods capable of contending with Him. So it is said to them in the manner of mockery (*tahakkum*). Just as He mocked them with the word *nidd*, He also condemned them for having set up many rivals for One who is not fit to have any rival at all.

Muhammad ibn al-Sumayfa' recited: "So do not set up for God a rival (*nidd*)."

**Question 3:** What is the meaning of ﴿while you know﴾?

The answer: its meaning is that you, by the perfection of your intellects, know that these things cannot be made rivals to God, the Exalted. So do not say that, for an ugly saying from one who knows its ugliness is even uglier.

Here there are issues.

**Issue 1:** Know that there is no one in the world who affirms for God a partner equal to Him in existence, power, knowledge and wisdom. This has not been found to this day. But the Dualists (*Thanawiyya*) affirm two gods: one is gentle and does good, and the second is foolish and does evil.

As for taking an object of worship other than God, the Exalted, there are many who hold this. The first group are the worshippers of the stars, and they are the Sabians (*Ṣābi'a*). They say that God, the Exalted, created these stars, and these stars are the governors of this world. They said: it is incumbent upon us to worship the stars, and the stars worship God, the Exalted. The second group are the Christians, who worship the Messiah, peace be upon him. The third group are the idol-worshippers.

Know that there is no religion more ancient than the religion of the idol-worshippers. That is because the earliest of the prophets whose history has been transmitted to us is Nuh (Noah), peace be upon him, and he came only to refute them, as God, the Exalted, has told us about his people in His saying: ﴿And they said: Do not leave your gods, nor leave Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth, nor Ya'uq, nor Nasr﴾ [Nuh: 23]. So we know that this assertion existed before Nuh, peace be upon him, and it remains to this day. Indeed, most of the people of the world persist in this assertion. A religion or doctrine of this nature cannot be such that its corruption is known by necessity. But the knowledge that this carved stone, at this moment, is not the one that created me and created the heavens and the earth is a necessary knowledge. So it is impossible for the great multitude to agree upon it. Therefore it must be that the idol-worshippers had another aim beyond that. The scholars have mentioned several aspects of this:

Page 104

First: what Abu Ma'shar Ja'far ibn Muhammad, the astrologer of Balkh, mentioned in some of his works, that many people of China and India believed in God and His angels, and held that God, the Exalted, is a body with a form, like the most beautiful of forms; and likewise the angels in their beautiful forms; and that they have all hidden themselves from us behind the sky; and that it is obligatory upon them to fashion images of elegant appearance and goodly aspect in the form that they believed to be the forms of God and the angels. Then they devoted themselves to worshipping them, seeking nearness to God and His angels. If what Abu Ma'shar mentioned is correct, then the cause of idol-worship is the belief in resemblance.

Second: what most scholars have mentioned, namely that people saw the changes in the states of this world linked to the changes in the states of the stars. For according to the nearness and distance of the sun from the zenith, different seasons and varying conditions arise. Then they observed the states of the rest of the stars and believed in the connection of happiness and misfortune in this world with the manner of their positions in people's horoscopes. When they believed that, they exaggerated in exalting them. Some of them believed that they are things necessarily existent in themselves, and that they are what created these worlds; and some believed that they are created by the Supreme God but that they are creators of this world. The first held that they are in reality God, and the second group held that they are the intermediaries between God, the Exalted, and mankind. So they inevitably occupied themselves with worshipping them and submitting to them. Then, when they saw the stars hidden for most of the time from sight, they took for them idols and devoted themselves to worshipping them, intending by those worships those lofty bodies and seeking nearness to their hidden forms. Then, when the period lengthened, they dropped mention of the stars and devoted themselves to worshipping those images. Such people are, in reality, worshippers of the stars.

Third: the practitioners of judgments (*aṣḥāb al-aḥkām*) used to specify times in the long-lasting years, some thousand or two thousand years, and claim that whoever makes a talisman (*ṭilsam*) at that time in a particular manner will benefit from it in specific conditions, such as happiness, abundance, and the averting of calamities. And when they made that talisman they venerated it, believing that they would benefit from it. When they exceeded in that veneration, it became like worship. And when the period of that practice lengthened, they forgot the beginning of the matter and occupied themselves with worshipping them in ignorance of the origin of the affair.

Fourth: whenever a great man among them died, whom they believed to be one whose supplication is answered and whose intercession is accepted with God, the Exalted, they took an idol in his likeness and worshipped it, on the belief that that person would be an intercessor for them on the Day of Resurrection before God, the Exalted, as God, the Exalted, has informed us of their saying in His words: ﴿These are our intercessors with God﴾ [Yunus: 18].

Fifth: perhaps they took them as prayer-niches (*maḥārīb*) for their prayers and acts of obedience, and prostrated towards them, not to them, just as we prostrate towards the qibla, not to the qibla. When this condition continued, the ignorant among the people thought that it was obligatory to worship them.

Sixth: perhaps they were among the anthropomorphists (*mujassima*), and believed in the permissibility of the Lord's indwelling in them, so they worshipped them on this interpretation.

These are the aspects by which this doctrine can be attributed to them, until it becomes such that its falsehood is known by the necessity of reason.
