**Issue 2:** If someone says: since the essence of the doctrine of the idol-worshippers reverts to these aspects you have mentioned, how does it follow from affirming the Creator of the world that the worship of idols is impermissible?

The answer: We say that God, the Exalted, only drew attention to the heavens and the earth being created by what we have explained, that the earth and the sky share with the rest of bodies in corporeality. So the distinction of each of them in the shapes, attributes and states it has must come from a specifier who specifies. We have explained that if that specifier were a body, it too would need another specifier, so it must not be a body.

Having established this, we say: as for the saying of those who went to the worship of idols on the basis of the belief in resemblance, since we have proven by this argument the negation of corporeality, their saying has been refuted. As for the second saying, namely that these stars are what govern this world, since we have established the proof that every body, in being characterised by everything it is characterised by, depends on the free and chosen agent, their being gods has been refuted, and it has been established that they are servants, not lords. As for the third saying, that of the masters of talismans, it has also been refuted, because the effect of talismans occurs only through the powers of the stars; and since we have demonstrated the createdness of the stars, our position is established and their position is refuted. As for the fourth and fifth sayings, there is nothing in reason that requires or makes impossible them; but since the law (*shar'*) has forbidden them, it is obligatory to refrain from them. As for the sixth saying, it too is based on anthropomorphism. So it has been established, by what we have presented, that establishing the proof of the world's dependence on the chosen Maker, who is exalted above corporeality, refutes the saying of worshipping idols on every interpretation. And God knows best.

\* \* \*

**Issue 3:** Know that before the going out of Alexander (*al-Iskandar*), the Greeks had undertaken to build temples for themselves known by the names of the spiritual powers and the luminous bodies, and they took them as objects of worship each separately. The temple of the First Cause, which for them is the Divine Command, and the temple of the Pure Intellect, and the temple of Absolute Governance, and the temple of the Soul and Form, were all circular. The temple of Saturn was hexagonal, the temple of Jupiter triangular, the temple of Mars oblong, the temple of the Sun quadrangular. The temple of Venus was triangular with a quadrangle within it, and the temple of Mercury was triangular with an oblong within it. The temple of the Moon was octagonal. The historians claim that 'Amr ibn Luhayy, when he became chief over his people and led their tiers, and took charge of the Sacred House, happened to make a journey to al-Balqa'. There he saw a people worshipping idols, and he asked them about them. They said: "These are lords whom we seek help from, and so we are helped, and we seek rain through them, and so we are given rain." So he requested of them that they honour him with one of them. They gave him the idol known as Hubal. He journeyed with it to Mecca, placed it in the Ka'ba, and called the people to venerate it. That was at the beginning of the reign of Shapur Dhu al-Aktaf.

Know that among the well-known idol-temples is "Ghamdan," which al-Dahhak built in the name of Venus (al-Zuhra) in the city of Sana'a, and which 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, destroyed. Among them is "Nawbahar of Balkh," which the king Manushahr built in the name of the moon (al-Qamar).

Then the tribes of the Arabs had well-known idols, such as "Wadd" at Dawmat al-Jandal for the tribe of Kalb; "Suwa'" for the Banu Hudhayl; "Yaghuth" for the Banu Madhhij; "Ya'uq" for Hamdan; "Nasr" in the land of Himyar for Dhu al-Kala'; "al-Lat" at al-Ta'if for Thaqif; "Manat" at Yathrib for the Khazraj; "al-'Uzza" for Kinanah in the regions of Makkah; and "Isaf and Na'ila" upon al-Safa and al-Marwah. Qusayy, the grandfather of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), used to forbid them from worshipping these and would call them to the worship of Allah the Exalted. Likewise was Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl, who is the one who says:

Is it one Lord, or a thousand lords, whom I worship, when affairs are divided?
I have abandoned al-Lat and al-'Uzza, both together,
Thus does the discerning man act.

**The Discussion of Prophethood**

﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant, then produce a surah like it, and call your witnesses besides God, if you are truthful. But if you do not, and you will never do it, then fear the Fire whose fuel is men and stones, prepared for the disbelievers.﴾

Regarding the verse, there are several issues.

**The First Issue:** Know that when the Exalted and Glorified established the conclusive proofs for the existence of the Creator and refuted the claim of a partner, He followed this with what indicates prophethood. This indicates the falsity of the view of the *Ta'limiyya* (the Ismaili-type group, "Instructionists," literally those who emphasize the teaching of an infallible Imam), who made knowledge of God depend on knowledge of the Messenger, and the view of the *Hashwiyya* (literally "the filling" or "the crude literalists," a derogatory term for those who take a literalist, anthropomorphic approach), who say that knowledge of God is attained only from the Qur'an and the reports. Since the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ is based on the Qur'an being miraculous, He established the proof that it is miraculous.

Know that its being miraculous can be explained by two methods.

**The First Method:** It may be said that this Qur'an must be in one of three states:

Either it is equal to the rest of the speech of eloquent speakers, or it exceeds the rest of the speech of eloquent speakers by a degree that does not break customary norms, or it exceeds them by a degree that does break them. The first two divisions are false, so the third is determined. We say that the first two are false because, if it were so, it would be obligatory for them to produce a surah like it, either together or individually. If there were dispute and fear of non-acceptance, then witnesses and judges would remove the doubt. This is the ultimate in argumentation, because they were supreme in knowledge of the language and in awareness of the rules of eloquence. They were also supremely eager to nullify his affair, to the point that they sacrificed their lives and wealth and endured every kind of destruction and trial. They were also so proud and zealous that they would not accept the truth, let alone falsehood. All of this requires that they produce something that would discredit his speech, and opposition is the strongest of discrediting. When they did not produce it, we knew their incapacity to do so. Thus it is established that the Qur'an does not resemble their speech, and that the difference between it and their speech is not an ordinary difference. Therefore it is a difference that breaks customary norms, and so it must be miraculous. This is the meaning of establishing this proof. It is thus clear that just as the Exalted did not rely on mere imitation (*taqlid*) for knowledge of monotheism, He did not rely on imitation for knowledge of prophethood.

Know that many features have gathered in the Qur'an that would seem to suggest a lack in its eloquence, yet it reached in eloquence a height beyond which there is no further height. This indicates that it is miraculous:

**First:** The eloquence of the Arabs consists mostly in describing observed things, such as describing a camel, a horse, a slave-girl, a king, a blow, a thrust, the description of a war, or the description of a raid. The Qur'an contains none of these things, so the eloquent words on which the Arabs agreed in their speech should not have been found in it.

**Second:** He, Exalted is He, observed the way of truthfulness and was free from falsehood in all of it. Every poet who abandoned falsehood and adhered to truth had his poetry come out weak and not good. Do you not see that Labid ibn Rabi'a and Hassan ibn Thabit, when they embraced Islam, their poetry declined, and their Islamic poetry was not as excellent as their pre-Islamic poetry? And God, Exalted is He, though He is free from falsehood and exaggeration, brought the Qur'an eloquent, as you see.

**Third:** Eloquent speech and eloquent poetry only occur in a qasida (ode) in a verse or two; the rest is not like that. The Qur'an is not like that, because all of it is eloquent to the degree that creatures are incapable of it, just as they were incapable of its whole.

**Fourth:** Whoever composes eloquent poetry describing a thing, if he repeats it, his second speech describing that thing does not stand on the level of his first speech. Yet the Qur'an contains much repetition, and each of its repetitions is at the peak of eloquence, and no difference at all appears.

**Fifth:** It restricted itself to prescribing acts of worship, prohibiting vices, urging noble character, abandoning this world and choosing the Hereafter, and such words reduce eloquence.

**Sixth:** They said: The poetry of Imru' al-Qays is good at times of joy, remembrance of women, and description of horses; the poetry of al-Nabigha is good in fear; the poetry of al-A'sha is good in seeking (gifts) and describing wine; the poetry of Zuhayr is good in desire and hope. In general, every poet's speech is good in one genre, and his speech weakens in other genres. As for the Qur'an, it came eloquent in all genres, at the utmost of eloquence. Do you not see that the Exalted and Glorified said in encouragement: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of the delight of the eyes﴾ [al-Sajda: 17], and He said: ﴿And therein is what the souls desire, and what the eyes delight in﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 71], and He said in warning: ﴿Do you feel secure that He will not cause the side of the land to swallow you?﴾ and the verses that follow [al-Isra: 68], and He said: ﴿Do you feel secure that He who is in heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you, and then it shakes?﴾ ﴿Or do you feel secure...﴾ the verse [al-Mulk: 16-17], and He said: ﴿And every obstinate tyrant has failed﴾ [Ibrahim: 15], up to His words: ﴿And death will come to him from every place﴾ [Ibrahim: 17], and He said in admonition what human imagination does not reach, which is His words: ﴿So each We seized for his sin﴾ [al-Ankabut: 40], up to His words: ﴿And among them are those We drowned﴾ [al-Ankabut: 40], and He said in exhortation what has no further increase: ﴿Have you considered, if We let them enjoy for years﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 205], and He said in matters of divinity: ﴿God knows what every female carries, and what the wombs diminish and what they increase﴾ to the end of it [al-Ra'd: 8].

**Seventh:** The Qur'an is the origin of all the sciences. All of the science of theology (*kalam*) is in the Qur'an; all of jurisprudence (*fiqh*) is derived from the Qur'an; likewise the science of the principles of jurisprudence, the science of grammar and language, the science of asceticism in this world, the reports of the Hereafter, and the practice of noble character. Whoever reflects on our book *Dala'il al-I'jaz* (*The Proofs of Inimitability*) will know that the Qur'an has reached the highest degree in all aspects of eloquence.

**The Second Method:** We say: The Qur'an either was at the level of eloquence that reaches inimitability, or it was not. If the first is true, it is established that it is miraculous. If the second is true, then opposition would be possible under this assumption. Their not producing an opposition, while opposition was possible, and while their motives to produce it were strong, is an event that breaks customary norms, and so that is miraculous. Thus it is established that the Qur'an is miraculous in all respects. This method, in our view, is closer to the correct position.

\* \* \*

**The Second Issue:** He said ﴿nazzalna﴾ ("We sent down") using the word *tanzil* (gradual sending down) rather than *inzal* (sending down all at once), because what is meant is descent by way of gradualness. The mention of this word is the most fitting in this place, because they used to say: "If this were from God, and different from what comes from people, it would not descend in this way, piece by piece, surah after surah, according to events and the occurrence of incidents, and in the manner we see of orators and poets, in whom what appears comes separately from time to time according to the changing circumstances and varying needs. A poet does not publish his collection of poetry all at once, nor does a writer of epistles and sermons publish his collection all at once. So if God sent it down, He would have sent it down in a manner contrary to this custom, all at once." ﴿And those who disbelieved said: Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?﴾ [al-Furqan: 32]. God, Exalted is He, here mentioned what indicates that the Qur'an is miraculous, together with what removes this doubt. Its explanation is that this Qur'an, sent down in this gradual manner, is either of the kind of what is within the power of humans or not. If the first, then it is obligatory for them to produce its like, or something close to it, gradually. If the second, then it is established that it is miraculous even though it was sent down gradually. It is read as ("on Our slaves"), meaning the Messenger of God ﷺ and his community.

\* \* \*

**The Third Issue:** The *surah* is a portion of the Qur'an. Its *waw* (the letter *w* in its root), if it is original, then it is either named after *sur* (the wall) of a city, which is its enclosure, because it is a bounded portion of the Qur'an like a walled town, or because it contains branches of knowledge just as the wall of a city contains what is in it. Or it is named after *surah* in the sense of rank, because a surah is like a station or grade through which the reader ascends, and in themselves surahs are long, medium, and short. Or it is named for the elevation of its rank and the greatness of its place in religion. If you make its *waw* a substitution for a *hamza*, then it is because it is a piece and a portion of the Qur'an, like the *su'r* which is the remainder of a thing and its surplus.

If it is said: What is the benefit of dividing the Qur'an into surahs? We say: For several reasons.

**First:** That for which authors divide their books into chapters and sections.

**Second:** When a genus has species beneath it, separating each species from its counterpart is better.

**Third:** When the reader finishes a surah or a chapter of the book and then begins another, it is more energizing for him and more firmly establishes his learning than if he continued through the book in its entirety. Similarly, a traveler who knows he has covered a mile or crossed a league feels relief from that and is encouraged to continue the journey.

**Fourth:** When the memorizer memorizes a surah, he believes he has taken from the Book of God a portion that is independent in itself, so he exalts that in his soul and rejoices in it. For this reason, reciting a complete surah in prayer is more excellent.

\* \* \*

**The Fourth Issue:** His saying ﴿so produce a surah like it﴾ indicates that the Qur'an, and its being in the form of surahs, is in the exact form that God, Exalted is He, sent down. This is contrary to the view of many of the people of hadith, who say that it was arranged in this order in the days of Uthman. Therefore the challenge was validly issued once with a surah and once with the whole Qur'an.

\* \* \*

**The Fifth Issue:** Know that the challenge with the Qur'an came in several forms:

**First:** His saying: ﴿Then produce a book from God that is better guidance than these two﴾ [al-Qasas: 49].

**Second:** His saying: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were helpers to one another﴾ [al-Isra: 88].

**Third:** His saying: ﴿Then produce ten surahs like it, fabricated﴾ [Hud: 13].

**Fourth:** His saying: ﴿So produce a surah like it.﴾ The parallel to this is someone who challenges his companion regarding his composition, saying: "Bring me its like; bring me its half; bring me its quarter; bring me one question from it." This is the ultimate in challenge and in removing excuses.

If it is said: His saying ﴿so produce a surah like it﴾ includes Surat al-Kawthar, Surat al-Asr, and Surat Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun. We know with certainty that producing its like, or something close to it, is possible. If you say that producing the like of such surahs is beyond human capacity, that would be obstinacy, and undertaking such obstinate claims opens an accusation against the religion. We say: For this very reason we chose the second method, and we said: If this surah reaches in eloquence the level of inimitability, then the purpose is achieved; and if the matter is not like that, then their abstention from opposition, despite the intensity of their motives to undermine his affair, is itself a miracle. On these two assumptions the miracle is realized.

\* \* \*

**The Sixth Issue:** To what does the pronoun in His saying ﴿its like﴾ refer? There are two views. One is that it refers to ("what") in His saying ﴿what We have sent down upon Our servant﴾, meaning: produce a surah of that which is of its quality in eloquence and beauty of arrangement. The second is that it refers to ("servant"), meaning: produce one from among one who is in his condition of being a human, unlettered, who did not read books and did not take from scholars. The first is transmitted from Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, and most of the verifiers. There are several considerations that favor it:

**First:** That this agrees with the rest of the verses that occur in the context of the challenge, especially what He mentioned in Yunus: ﴿then produce a surah like it﴾ [Yunus: 38].

وثانيها: أنَّ البحث إنما وقع في المُنزَّل، لأنه قال: ﴿وإن كنتم في ريب مما نزَّلنا﴾ (وإن كنتم في شك مما أنزلناه)، فوجب صرف الضمير إليه. ألا ترى أن المعنى: وإن ارتبتم في أن القرآن مُنزَّل من عند الله، فهاتوا شيئًا مما يماثله. ومقتضى الترتيب، لو كان الضمير مردودًا إلى رسول الله ﷺ، أن يُقال: وإن ارتبتم في أن محمدًا مُنزَّل عليه، فهاتوا قرآنًا من مثله.

وثالثها: أنَّ الضمير لو كان عائدًا إلى القرآن لاقتضى كونهم عاجزين عن الإتيان بمثله، سواء اجتمعوا أو انفردوا، وسواء كانوا أميين أو كانوا عالمين محصِّلين. أما لو كان عائدًا إلى محمد ﷺ، فذلك لا يقتضي إلا كون أحدهم من الأميين عاجزين عنه، لأنه لا يكون مثل محمد إلا الشخص الواحد الأمي. فأما لو اجتمعوا وكانوا قارئين، لم يكونوا مثل محمد، لأن الجماعة لا تماثل الواحد، والقارئ لا يكون مثل الأمي، ولا شك أن الإعجاز على الوجه الأول أقوى.

ورابعها: أنا لو صرفنا الضمير إلى القرآن، فكونه مُعجِزًا (الإعجاز: عجز الخلق عن الإتيان بمثله) إنما يحصل لكمال حاله في الفصاحة. أما لو صرفناه إلى محمد ﷺ، فكونه مُعجِزًا إنما يكمل بتقرير كمال حاله في كونه أميًّا بعيدًا عن العلم. وهذا وإن كان مُعجِزًا أيضًا، إلا أنه لما كان لا يتم إلا بتقرير نوع من النقصان في حق محمد ـ عليه السلام ـ كان الأول أولى.

وخامسها: أنا لو صرفنا الضمير إلى محمد ـ عليه السلام ـ لكان ذلك يوهم أن صدور مثل القرآن ممن لم يكن مثل محمد في كونه أميًّا مُمكنٌ، ولو صرفناه إلى القرآن لدلَّ ذلك على أن صدور مثله من الأمي وغير الأمي مُمتنِع، فكان هذا أولى.

**المسألة السابعة:** في المراد من الشهداء وجهان:

الأول: المراد مَن ادَّعَوا فيه الإلهية، وهي الأوثان. فكأنه قيل لهم: إن كان الأمر كما تقولون، من أنها تستحق العبادة لِما أنها تنفع وتضر، فقد دُفعتم في منازعة محمد ﷺ إلى فاقة شديدة وحاجة عظيمة في التخلص عنها، فتعجَّلوا الاستعانة بها، وإلا فاعلموا أنكم مُبطلون في ادعاء كونها آلهة وأنها تنفع وتضر. فيكون في الكلام محاجَّة من وجهين: أحدهما في إبطال كونها آلهة، والثاني: في إبطال ما أنكروه من إعجاز القرآن وأنه من قِبَله.

الثاني: المراد من الشهداء أكابرهم، أو من يوافقهم في إنكار أمر محمد ـ عليه السلام ـ. والمعنى: وادعوا أكابركم ورؤساءكم ليعينوكم على المعارضة، وليحكموا لكم وعليكم فيما يمكن ويتعذر. فإن قيل: هل يمكن
