First issue: whoever holds that Adam's Garden was in the heavens interprets the descent (hubut) as coming down from a higher place to a lower one. Whoever holds that it was on the earth interprets it as moving from one place to another, like His words: ﴿Go down to a city [Egypt]﴾ [al-Baqarah: 61].

Second issue: they differed about who is addressed by this command, though they agree that Adam and Eve, peace be upon them, were addressed by it. They gave several views:

The first, which is the view of most, is that Iblis is also included. They said: because Iblis's mention has preceded in His words ﴿so the Satan caused them to slip from it﴾, meaning: he caused them to slip, and We said to them, "Go down."

* * *

As for His words ﴿some of you are enemies to others﴾, this is a description to Adam and Eve, peace be upon them, that Iblis is an enemy to them and to their offspring, just as He had informed them of this before eating from the tree, when He said: ﴿So We said, "O Adam, this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not expel you from the Garden, for then you would be distressed"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 117]. If it is said: when Iblis refused to prostrate, he became a disbeliever and was expelled from the Garden, and it was said to him: ﴿Go down from it, for it is not for you to be arrogant therein﴾ [al-A'raf: 13], and He also said: ﴿So get out from it, for indeed you are expelled﴾ [al-Hijr: 34]. He was brought down from it only because of his arrogance. Adam's slip happened long after that, and then he was commanded to go down because of the slip. Since Iblis's descent occurred before that, how can His words ﴿Go down﴾ include him? We say: when God brought him down to the earth, perhaps he returned to the heavens once more in order to whisper to Adam and Eve. When Adam and Eve were in the Garden, God said to them: ﴿Go down﴾ [Ta-Ha: 123]. When they left the Garden and Iblis gathered with them outside the Garden, He commanded all of them, saying: ﴿Go down.﴾ Some people said: the meaning of His words ﴿Go down﴾ is not that He said it to them all at once, but that He said it to each one of them separately, at a time.

The second view: the intended ones are Adam, Eve and the serpent. This view is weak, because it is established by consensus that the mukallafun (those responsible under religious law) are the angels, the jinn and humankind. An objector may dispute this consensus, for some people say that a group of responsible beings may exist among others, as He said: ﴿Each has known its prayer and its glorification﴾ [al-Nur: 41], and Solomon said to the hoopoe: ﴿I will surely punish him with a severe punishment﴾ [al-Naml: 21].

The third view: the intended ones are Adam, Eve and their offspring, because since they were the origin of humankind, they were treated as if they were all of humankind. The evidence for this is His words ﴿Go down, some of you enemies to others﴾, and it is also indicated by His words: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve. And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever﴾ [al-Baqarah: 38–39]. This is a ruling that covers all people. The meaning of ﴿some of you are enemies to others﴾ is the mutual hostility and hatred among people and their misguiding one another. Know that this view is weak, because the offspring did not exist at that time, so how could the address include them? As for one who claims that the minimum plural is two, the objection does not apply to his view.

Third issue: they differed over whether His words ﴿Go down﴾ are a command or a permission. The more likely view is that it is a command, because it contains great hardship: leaving what they were in, the Garden, for a place where livelihood is attainable only through hardship and toil, is among the hardest of obligations. Once this is established, the notion that it is a punishment is invalidated, because hardship in obligation is a cause of reward, so how could it be a punishment given the great benefit it contains? If it is said: do you not say that the prescribed punishments (hudud) and many expiations (kaffarat) are punishments, although they belong to the category of obligations? We say: as for the prescribed punishments, they fall upon the one who is punished through the act of another, so they may be a punishment if the person persists in the offence. As for expiations, it is said of some of them only that they operate as punishments, because they are not established except together with sin. But that they should be a punishment while being occasions for great reward is not so.

Fourth issue: His words ﴿Go down, some of you enemies to others﴾ are a command to descend, not a command to enmity, because Iblis's enmity toward Adam and Eve arose from envy and arrogance toward prostration, and from his deceiving them until he expelled them from the Garden, and his enmity toward their offspring through casting whispers and calling to disbelief and disobedience. None of this may be commanded. But Adam's enmity toward Iblis is commanded, by His words: ﴿Indeed the Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy﴾ [Fatir: 6], and His words: ﴿O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from the Garden﴾ [al-A'raf: 27]. Once this is established, it becomes clear that the meaning of the verse is: go down from the heavens, while some of you are enemies to others.

Fifth issue: "al-mustaqarr" may mean the act of settling, as in His words: ﴿To your Lord that day is the mustaqarr﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 12], and it may mean the place where one settles, as in His words: ﴿The companions of the Garden that day are better in mustaqarr﴾ [al-Furqan: 24], and He said: ﴿So there is a mustaqarr and a mustawda'﴾ [al-An'am: 98]. Given this, most scholars understood His words ﴿And for you on the earth is a mustaqarr﴾ [al-Baqarah: 36; al-A'raf: 24] as referring to a place, and the meaning is that it is your settling place during the states of life and death. Al-Suddi narrated from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he said: the mustaqarr is the grave, that is, your graves in which you will be. The first is preferable, because He appointed the enjoyment (mata'), and that suits only the state of life. And because He addressed them with this at the time of the descent, which implies the state of life.

Know that in Surat al-A'raf, in this same story, He said: ﴿He said, "Go down, some of you enemies to others. And for you on the earth is a mustaqarr and enjoyment for a time."﴾ ﴿He said, "Therein you will live, therein you will die, and from it you will be brought forth."﴾ [al-A'raf: 24–25]. It is possible that His words ﴿Therein you will live﴾, to the end of the statement, are an explanation of His words ﴿And for you on the earth is a mustaqarr and enjoyment for a time﴾, and it is possible that they are an addition to the first.

Sixth issue: they differed over the meaning of "hin" (a time), though they agree that it is a noun for time. The preferable view is that it refers to an extended span of time, because a man says to his companion, "I have not seen you for a hin," when his seeing him has been long delayed, and one does not say this when they have recently met. Since human lifespans are long, and their deaths are far from the beginnings of their existence, it was permissible to say: ﴿And enjoyment for a time﴾.

Seventh issue: know that in these verses there is a great warning against all sins, in several respects.

The first: whoever contemplates what befell Adam, peace be upon him, because of his taking this small slip, will be in great fear of sins. The poet said:

O you who gazes with the eye of one asleep, and witnesses the matter without really witnessing:
You join sins to sins, yet you hope to attain the gardens and the victory of the worshipper.
Have you forgotten that God expelled Adam from it to this world because of a single sin?

And it is narrated from Fath al-Mawsili that he said: "We were a people from the people of the Garden, then Iblis took us captive into this world, and there is nothing for us but worry and grief until we are returned to the abode from which we were expelled."

The second: a warning against arrogance, envy and greed. Qatada, regarding His words ﴿he refused and was arrogant﴾ [al-Baqarah: 34], said: "The enemy of God, Iblis, envied Adam for the honour God had given him, and said: 'I am from fire, and he is from clay.' Then he cast greed into Adam's heart until it moved him to commit what was forbidden. Then he cast envy into the heart of Qabil (Cain) until he killed Habil (Abel)."

The third: He, glory be to Him, made clear the severe enmity between the offspring of Adam and Iblis, and this is a great reminder of the obligation to be wary.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on Surah 2, verse 37 (part 1 of 3):**

Allah's words: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He turned to him in forgiveness. Indeed He is the Oft-Returning, the Most Merciful.﴾ On this verse there are several issues.

**The first issue:** Al-Qaffal said: The original meaning of *talaqqi* (receiving) is to go out to meet something, and then it is used for the position of receiving something that comes, and then for the sense of accepting and taking. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And indeed you receive the Qur'an from One who is Wise and All-Knowing﴾ [al-Naml: 6], meaning, you are taught it. It is said: "We went out to receive the pilgrims," meaning we met them. It is said: "I received this word from so-and-so," meaning I took it from him. Since this is the root meaning, and whoever meets a man and they meet each other, each one meets the other, so the act of meeting is attributed to both together, it is valid for both to share this description. Thus it is said: "Whatever you received, it has also received you." So it is permissible to say: "Adam received words," meaning he took them, understood them, and accepted them with acceptance. It is also permissible to read *talaqqa* with *kalimatun* in the nominative (*talaqqa kalimatun*), meaning words came to him from Allah. A similar usage is His saying: ﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 124]. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is recited as *al-zalimun* (nominative plural).

**The second issue:** It is stated that it is not permissible that the meaning is that Allah taught him the reality of repentance (*tawbah*, turning back to Allah), because the one who is legally responsible must know the nature of repentance, be able through it to make amends for sins, and distinguish it from other things, let alone the prophets, peace be upon them. Rather, this must be interpreted as one of the following:

First: The alerting of him to the sin committed by him, in such a way that at that point Adam, peace be upon him, became one of those who repent and turn back penitently.

Second: That Allah informed him of the obligation of repentance and that it is inevitably accepted, meaning that whoever commits a sin, small or great, then regrets what he did and resolves not to return to it, I will certainly accept his repentance. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words﴾, meaning he took them, accepted them, and acted upon them.

Third: That Allah reminded him of His great blessings upon him, so that this became a strong motive toward repentance.

Fourth: That Allah taught him words which, if repentance were accompanied by them, would be a cause of the perfection of the state of repentance.

* * *

**The third issue:** They differed over what those words were. Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that Adam, peace be upon him, said: "O Lord, did You not create me with Your own hand, without intermediary?" He said: "Yes." He said: "O Lord, did You not breathe into me of Your spirit?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Did You not settle me in Your Garden?" He said: "Yes." He said: "O Lord, did Your mercy not precede Your wrath?" He said: "Yes." He said: "O Lord, if I repent and reform, will You return me to the Garden?" He said: "Yes." This is His saying: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words﴾. Al-Suddi added to it: "O Lord, did You not write a sin against me?" He said: "Yes."

Second: Al-Nakha'i said: I came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: "What are the words that Adam received from his Lord?" He said: Allah taught Adam and Hawwa' (Eve) the rites of the Hajj, so they performed the Hajj, and these are the words that are said in the Hajj. When they finished the Hajj, Allah the Exalted revealed to them that He had accepted their repentance.

Third: Mujahid and Qatadah, in one of the two narrations from them, said: They are His saying: ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers﴾ [al-A'raf: 23].

Fourth: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they are: "There is no god but You, glory be to You, and praise be to You. I have done evil and wronged myself, so forgive me, for You are the best of forgivers. There is no god but You, glory be to You, and praise be to You. I have done evil and wronged myself, so have mercy on me, for You are the best of the merciful. There is no god but You, glory be to You, and praise be to You. I have done evil and wronged myself, so turn to me in forgiveness, for You are the Oft-Returning, the Most Merciful."

Fifth: 'Aishah said: When Allah wished to turn to Adam in forgiveness, he circumambulated the House seven times, and the House at that time was a red mound. When he had prayed two rak'ahs, he faced the House and said: "O Allah, You know my secret and my open affairs, so accept my excuse. You know my need, so grant me my request. You know what is in my soul, so forgive me my sins. O Allah, I ask You for a faith that penetrates my heart and a true certainty, until I know that nothing will befall me except what You have written for me, and that I am content with what You have apportioned to me." Then Allah the Exalted revealed to Adam: "O Adam, I have forgiven you your sin, and no one from your offspring will come to Me and call upon Me with this supplication that you have called upon Me with, except that I will forgive his sin, relieve his distresses and sorrows, remove poverty from between his eyes, and the world will come to him while he does not desire it."

* * *

**The fourth issue:** Al-Ghazali, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Repentance is realized through three matters that follow one another in order: knowledge, state, and action. Knowledge comes first, the state second, and action third. The first necessitates the second, and the second necessitates the third, a necessitation required by the sunnah (established pattern) of Allah in the dominion and the unseen realm. As for knowledge, it is the awareness of the harm in the sin and that it is a veil between the servant and the mercy of the Lord. When he knows this with certain knowledge, there arises from this knowledge a pain in the heart due to the loss of the beloved. The heart, whenever it perceives the loss of the beloved, feels pain. If that loss is caused by his own doing, he grieves over the action that was the cause of that loss, and this grief is called *nadam* (regret). Then, when that pain intensifies, a firm resolve arises from it, and this resolve is related to the present, the future, and the past. As for its relation to the present, it is by abandoning the sin that he was engaged in. As for the future, it is the determination to abandon that action which causes the loss of the beloved until the end of his life. As for the past, it is by making up for what has passed through compensation and making up, if it is capable of compensation. So knowledge is the first, and it is the dawn of these goods, and by it I mean complete certainty that these sins are deadly poisons. This certainty is a light, and this light produces the fire of regret, so the heart is pained by it, when through the radiance of the light of faith it perceives that it has become veiled from its beloved, like one upon whom the light of the sun shines, having been in darkness, when the light rises upon him by the clearing of the clouds, and he sees his beloved has come near to destruction. Then the fires of love ignite in his heart, and from those fires there arises his will to rise and make amends. So knowledge, regret, and the intention related to abstaining in the present and the future, and making up for the past, are three meanings that follow one another in coming into being (for repentance). The name *tawbah* is applied to the whole of them, and very often the name *tawbah* is applied to the meaning of regret alone, and prior knowledge is considered like a preliminary, and abstention like the fruit and the subsequent follower. With this consideration, the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Regret is repentance," since regret is never separated from a knowledge that caused it or from a resolve that follows it, so regret is enclosed by its two ends, meaning what produces it and its fruit. This is what Shaykh al-Ghazali summarized concerning the reality of repentance, and it is a good statement.

Al-Qaffal said: Repentance must include abandoning that sin, regret for what has passed, resolve not to return to its like, and apprehensive fear throughout all of this. As for the necessity of abandonment: if he does not abandon it, he would still be doing it, and so he would not be repentant. As for regret: if he does not regret, he would be content with having done it, and one who is content with a thing may do it, while one who does a thing is not repentant of it. As for the resolve not to return to its like: his doing it was a disobedience, and resolving upon disobedience is itself disobedience. As for apprehensive fear: he is commanded to repent, and he has no way to be certain that he has performed repentance as it was required of him, so he remains fearful. For this reason Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He fears the Hereafter and hopes for the mercy of his Lord﴾ [al-Zumar: 9]. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "If the fear and hope of the believer were weighed, they would balance."

Know that al-Ghazali's statement, may Allah have mercy on him, is clearer and more penetrating in verification. However, a problem arises for it, namely that knowledge that a particular act is harmful, together with knowledge that this act proceeded from him, necessitates pain in the heart, and that pain necessitates the will to abandon it in the present and future, and the will to make up for what he did in the past. If some of these things are necessarily ordered upon others, then that is not within his power, and it would be impossible for him to be commanded with it.

The conclusion is that what falls within one's capacity is only acquiring knowledge; as for everything beyond that, choice has no path to it. But one may say: acquiring knowledge is also not within one's capacity, because acquiring knowledge of some unknown matters is not possible except through known matters prior to that unknown. Those present knowns, by which one reaches the acquisition of that unknown, either necessarily entail knowledge of that unknown or do not entail it. If the first, then the ordering of what is reached upon what is used to reach it is necessary, and so it is not within capacity and choice. If the second, then the deduction of the sought unknown from those present knowns does not follow, because the nearest premises must be such that accepting them in the mind necessitates accepting the conclusion; if they are not so, then those premises do not produce that conclusion. If it is said: Why is it not permissible to say that those premises, though present in the mind, the manner of reaching that conclusion from them is not present in the mind, and therefore knowledge of those premises does not necessarily entail knowledge of that conclusion? We reply: knowledge of the manner of reaching that conclusion from them is either among self-evident truths or among acquired truths. If it is among self-evident truths, it is not within one's capacity. If it is among acquired truths, the discussion concerning how it is acquired is as in the first case, so either it leads to an infinite regress, which is impossible, or it becomes one of its necessary consequences, and the problem mentioned returns. And Allah knows best.

* * *

**The fifth issue:** The Qadi 'Abd al-Jabbar posed a question to himself, saying: If this disobedience is minor (*saghirah*), how is repentance obligatory? He answered that Abu 'Ali (al-Jubba'i) said: It is obligatory upon him because the legally responsible person, once he knows he has disobeyed, is not free from it thereafter, and he is free in his choice, and there is nothing preventing him from being regretful or persistent. But persistence is ugly, so he cannot fully separate himself from this ugliness except through repentance. Therefore it is obligatory in either case, whether the disobedience was minor or major, and whether he recalled it having already repented of it earlier or had not repented. As for Abu Hashim, he permits that the disobedient person may be free of both repentance and persistence, and he says: It is not valid that repentance is obligatory upon the prophets for this reason. Rather, it must be obligatory for one of several reasons: either it is obligatory because by the minor sin their reward has been reduced, and that reduction is restored by repentance; or because repentance is considered equivalent to abandonment, so if abandonment is obligatory when possible, then repentance must also be obligatory when abandonment is not possible. He sometimes said: repentance is obligatory upon them on the basis of revelation (*sam'*), and this is the most correct view according to his position, because repentance cannot be obligatory merely for the return of reward, which consists only of benefits, since an act cannot be obligatory for the sake of attracting benefits, just as supererogatory acts are not obligatory. Rather, when Allah the Exalted protected the prophets, peace be upon them, one of the causes of their protection became the strictness upon them regarding repentance, state after state, even if their disobediences were minor.

* * *

**The sixth issue:** Al-Qaffal said: The root of *tawbah* (repentance) is return, like *awbah*. It is said *taba* just as it is said *aba*. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Acceptor of repentance﴾ [Ghafir: 3]. So their saying *taba yatubu tawban wa tawbatan wa mataban*, and *fahuwa ta'ib wa tawwab*, is like their saying *aba ya'ubu awban wa awbatan*, and *fahuwa a'ib wa awwab*. *Tawbah* is a word shared by the Lord and the servant. When it is applied to the servant, the meaning is that he returned to his Lord, because every disobedient person is in the state of one who flees from his Lord. When he repents, he has turned back from his flight to his Lord, so it is said: *taba ila rabbihi* (he repented to his Lord). In this case the Lord is like one who turns away from His servant. When it is applied to the Exalted Lord, the meaning is that He returned to His servant with His mercy and grace. For this reason the construction differs: it is said of the servant *taba ila rabbihi* (he repented to his Lord), and of the Lord *taba 'ala 'abdihi* (He turned toward His servant). A man may leave the service of a ruler, and the ruler then withdraws his favour from him. Afterwards the man resumes his service, and it is said: "So-and-so returned to the amir, and the amir returned to him with his kindness and favour." Having understood this, we say: the acceptance of repentance occurs in two ways:
First: that He rewards it with a great reward, just as the acceptance of obedience is meant in that sense.
Second: that He forgives his sins because of the repentance.

***

**The seventh issue:** What is meant by describing Allah the Exalted as *Tawwab* is intensity in accepting repentance, and this is in two respects:
The first: whenever one of the kings of this world is wronged by a person and that person then apologises to him, the king accepts the apology. But if the person returns to the wrong and to apologising a second time, the king does not accept it, because his nature prevents him from accepting excuses. Allah, glorified and exalted, is not like that. He accepts repentance not for any reason related to softness of nature, nor to bring benefit or ward off harm, but purely out of beneficence and bounty. Even if a responsible person disobeys every hour, then repents, and remains in this state for a long life, Allah the Exalted would still forgive him what has passed and accept his repentance. Thus He deserves intensity in accepting repentance, and so He is described as *Tawwab*.
The second: those who repent to Allah the Exalted are many, so if He accepts the repentance of all of them, He deserves intensity in this. Since accepting repentance together with the removal of punishment requires the attainment of reward, and since reward from Him is a blessing and a mercy, He described Himself, along with being *Tawwab*, as *Raheem* (Most Merciful).

***

**The eighth issue:** In this verse there are several benefits.

**The first benefit:** The servant must be occupied with repentance at every moment and time, because of the hadiths and reports that have come concerning this.

As for the hadiths:
(a) It is related that a man asked the Commander of the Faithful, ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, about a man who sins and then seeks forgiveness, then sins and seeks forgiveness, then sins and seeks forgiveness. The Commander of the Faithful said: "He should keep seeking forgiveness forever, until Satan is the one who loses and says: 'I have no strength against him.'" ʿAli also said: "Whenever you can throw him into a predicament and escape from it, then do so."

(b) Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, related that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "One who seeks forgiveness does not persist in sin, even if he returns to it seventy times in a day."

(c) From Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Repent to your Lord, for I repent to Him a hundred times every day."

(d) Abu Hurayrah said: When the Prophet, peace be upon him, was sent down the verse ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ [al-Shuʿara: 214], he said: "O assembly of Quraysh, buy yourselves from Allah; I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O ʿAbbas ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O Safiyyah, aunt of the Messenger of Allah, I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, ask me for whatever you wish; I cannot avail you anything against Allah." It was transmitted by the two Shaykhs in their *Sahihs*.

(e) The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, there comes a veil over my heart, so I seek Allah's forgiveness a hundred times a day."

Know that *ghayn* is something that covers the heart and conceals it to some extent. It is like a thin cloud that passes through the sky, which does not block the sun but prevents its full light. Then they gave several interpretations of this hadith:
First: Allah the Exalted informed His Prophet of what would happen among his community after him of disagreements and afflictions. Whenever he mentioned that, he found a cloud in his heart, so he sought forgiveness for his community.
Second: He, peace be upon him, was moving from one state to a state higher than the first, so the seeking of forgiveness was for that.
Third: The cloud is an expression of the intoxication that befell him on the path of love, until he became completely annihilated from himself. When he returned to sobriety, the seeking of forgiveness was for that sobriety. This is the interpretation of the people of inner realities (*ahl al-haqiqah*).
Fourth: This is the interpretation of the literalists (*ahl al-zahir*): the heart is never free of passing thoughts, impulses, desires, and various inclinations and wills, so he would seek help from the Lord, the Exalted, in repelling those thoughts.

(f) Abu Hurayrah said: ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said regarding the words of the Exalted ﴿Repent to Allah with sincere repentance﴾ [al-Tahrim: 8]: it is that a man commits a sin, then repents, not wanting to commit it again and not returning to it. Ibn Masʿud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: it is that he abandons the sin and resolves never to return to it.

(g) The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) related from Allah the Exalted, saying that He says to His angels: "When My servant intends a good deed, write it down for him as one good deed. If he does it, write it down as ten like it. When he intends an evil deed and then does it, write it down as one evil deed. But if he abandons it, write it down for him as a good deed." Narrated by Muslim.

(h) It is related that Gabriel, peace be upon him, heard Abraham, peace be upon him, saying: "O Generous in pardon!" Gabriel said: "Do you know what generous pardon is?" He said: "No, O Gabriel." He said: "It is that He pardons the evil deed and records it as a good deed."

(i) Abu Hurayrah related from him, peace be upon him: "Whoever begins his day with good and ends it with good, Allah the Exalted says to the angels: 'Do not write down against My servant the sins that lie between them.'"

(j) From Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, who said: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Among those before you there was a man who had killed ninety-nine souls. He asked about the most knowledgeable person on earth, and was directed to a monk. He came to him and said: 'Indeed I have killed ninety-nine souls; is there any repentance for the killer?' He said: 'No.' So he killed him, completing a hundred. Then he asked about the most knowledgeable person on earth, and was directed to a learned man. He came to him and said: 'Indeed I have killed a hundred souls; is there any repentance for me?' He said: 'Yes, and who can stand between you and repentance? Go to such-and-such a land, for there are people there who worship Allah the Exalted; worship Him with them, and do not return to your land, for it is a land of evil.' So he set out, and when he reached halfway, death came to him. The angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed over him. The angels of mercy said: 'He came repentant, turning with his heart to Allah the Exalted.' The angels of punishment said: 'He never did a single good deed.' Then an angel came to them in the form of a human and stood between them, and said: 'Measure the distance between the two lands; whichever he is nearer to, he belongs to it.' They measured, and they found him nearer by a span to the land he had intended, so the angels of mercy took him." Narrated by Muslim.

(k) Thabit al-Bunani said: It has reached us that Iblis said: "O Lord, You created Adam and placed enmity between me and him; so empower me over him and his offspring." Allah the Exalted said: "I have made their breasts dwellings for you." He said: "O Lord, increase me." He said: "No child is born to Adam except that ten are born to you." He said: "O Lord, increase me." He said: "They will flow in him as blood flows." He said: "O Lord, increase me." He said: ﴿Incite against them your cavalry and your infantry, and share with them in wealth and children﴾ [al-Isra: 64]. Then Adam complained about Iblis to his Lord, the Exalted, and said: "O Lord, You created Iblis, placed enmity and hatred between me and him, and empowered him over me and my offspring, and I cannot withstand him except by You." Allah the Exalted said: "No child will be born to you except that I will assign to him two angels to guard him from evil companions." He said: "O Lord, increase me." He said: "A good deed is multiplied tenfold." He said: "O Lord, increase me." He said: "I will not withhold repentance from any of your children as long as he has not reached the death rattle."

(l) Abu Musa al-Ashʿari said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed Allah the Exalted extends His hand at night so that the one who sinned by day may repent, and by day so that the one who sinned by night may repent, until the sun rises from its west." Narrated by Muslim.

(m) From ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Whenever I heard a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah benefited me from it as He willed. When one of his companions related to me, I made him swear, and if he swore to me, I believed him. Abu Bakr related to me, and Abu Bakr spoke truly. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No servant commits a sin, then performs ablution well, then stands and prays two rak'ahs and seeks forgiveness from Allah the Exalted, except that He forgives him." Then he recited: ﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves...﴾ up to His words ﴿...and seek forgiveness for their sins﴾ [Al ʿImran: 135].

(n) Abu Umamah said: "While I was sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), a man came to him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have committed a hadd offence, so establish it upon me.' He turned away from him, then the man returned and said the same thing. The prayer was called, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered, prayed, then went out." Abu Umamah said: "I was walking with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while the man followed him saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have committed a hadd offence, so establish it upon me.' He, peace be upon him, said: 'Did you not, when you left your house, perform ablution and do it well?' He said: 'Yes, O Messenger.' He said: 'And did you witness this prayer with us?' He said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Then indeed Allah has forgiven your hadd, or said your sin.'" Narrated by Muslim.

(o) ʿAbd Allah said: "A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I had an encounter with a woman from the far end of Medina, and I came close to her without touching her. Here I am; decide my case as you will.' ʿUmar said to him: 'Allah would have concealed you had you concealed yourself.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave him no reply. The man rose and went off, but the Prophet (ﷺ) called him back and recited to him this verse: ﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and in the first hours of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾ [Hud: 114]. One of the people said: 'O Prophet of Allah, is this for him alone?' He said: 'Rather, it is for people in general.'" Narrated by Muslim.

(p) Abu Hurayrah said: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, a servant committed a sin and said: 'O Lord, I have sinned, so forgive me.' His Lord said: 'My servant knows that he has a Lord who forgives sin and takes account for it, so I have forgiven My servant.' Then he remained as long as Allah willed, then committed another sin and said: 'O Lord, I have sinned again, so forgive me.' His Lord said: 'My servant knows that he has a Lord who forgives sin and takes account for it, so I have forgiven My servant.' Then he remained as long as Allah willed, then committed another sin and said: 'O Lord, I have sinned another sin, so forgive me.' His Lord said: 'My servant knows that he has a Lord who forgives sin and takes account for it. I have forgiven My servant, so let him do whatever he wishes.'" Both Shaykhs transmitted it in their *Sahihs*.

(q) Abu Bakr said: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "One who seeks forgiveness from Allah does not persist in sin, even if he returns to it seventy times in a day."

(r) Abu Ayyub said: "I had concealed something from you that I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: 'Were it not that you sin and then seek forgiveness, Allah the Exalted would create a people who sin and then seek forgiveness, and He would forgive them.'" Narrated by Muslim.

(يط) ʿAbdullah said: "While we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a man came up to him wearing a cloak, and in his hand was something wrapped in it. He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I passed by a thicket of trees and heard the sounds of baby birds, so I took them and placed them in my cloak. Then their mother came and circled over my head, so I uncovered them for her, and their mother descended upon them, so I wrapped them all together in my cloak, and they are with me.' The Prophet ﷺ, peace be upon him, said: 'Put them down from you.' So he put them down, but their mother refused except to stay with them. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: 'Do you marvel at the mercy of the mother bird for her young?' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, or he said: By Him who sent me with the truth as a prophet, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is more merciful to His servants than the mother bird is to her young. Return them to where you took them, and their mother with them.' So he returned them."

(k) From Abu Muslim al-Khawlani, from Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, from Jibril (peace be upon him), from Allah, glorified and exalted, who said: "O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another. O My servants, you err by night and by day, and I am the One who forgives sins and I do not mind, so seek forgiveness from Me and I will forgive you. O My servants, all of you are hungry except those whom I have fed, so seek food from Me and I will feed you. O My servants, all of you are naked except those whom I have clothed, so seek clothing from Me and I will clothe you. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the heart of the most righteous man among you, that would not increase in My dominion anything. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the heart of the most wicked man among you, that would not decrease in My dominion anything. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, gathered in one open place and asked Me, and I gave each person among you what he asked, that would not decrease in My dominion anything except as a needle decreases the sea when it is dipped in it once. O My servants, it is only your deeds that I record for you and then repay you for; so whoever finds good, let him praise Allah, and whoever finds other than that, let him blame none but himself."

He said: Abu Idris, whenever he narrated this hadith, would drop to his knees out of reverence for it.

As for the reports: Dhu al-Nun was asked about repentance (tawbah), and he said: "It is a comprehensive term for six meanings:
The first: regret for what has passed.
The second: resolve to abandon sins in the future.
The third: rendering every obligation you neglected between you and Allah, Exalted.
The fourth: restoring rights of injustice to the creatures, in their wealth and their honour.
The fifth: melting away every flesh and blood that grew from the unlawful.
The sixth: making the body taste the pain of acts of obedience just as it tasted the sweetness of disobedience."

Ahmad ibn Haris used to say: "O companion of sins, has it not come time for you to repent? O companion of sins, indeed the sin is written in the register. O companion of sins, you are in the grave distressed because of it. O companion of sins, you will be sought for your sins tomorrow."

The second benefit of the verse: Since Adam, peace be upon him, did not dispense with repentance despite his high rank, one of us is more deserving of it.

The third benefit: What appeared from Adam, peace be upon him, of weeping over his slip is also a warning for us, because we are more deserving of weeping than Adam, peace be upon him. It was reported from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "If the weeping of the people of the world were gathered together with the weeping of Dawud, the weeping of Dawud would be greater. If the weeping of the people of the world and the weeping of Dawud were gathered together with the weeping of Nuh, the weeping of Nuh would be greater. If the weeping of the people of the world and the weeping of Dawud and the weeping of Nuh, peace be upon them, were gathered together with the weeping of Adam over his error, the weeping of Adam would be greater."

The ninth issue: Allah, Exalted, mentioned only the repentance of Adam and not the repentance of Hawwa' because she was a follower of him, just as mention of women is omitted in the Qur'an and the Sunnah for this reason. He did mention her in His saying: ﴿They said: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves﴾ [al-A'raf: 23].

[p. 26]

**His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We said, "Go down from it, all of you. And if guidance comes to you from Me, then whoever follows My guidance, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve."﴾** In it are several issues.

**First issue:** They mentioned two explanations for the purpose of repeating the command to descend:

The first: al-Jubba'i (al-Jubba'i) said: the first descent is not the second. The first is from the Garden to the lowest heaven, and the second is from the lowest heaven to the earth. This view is weak for two reasons.

One: He said in the first descent, ﴿And for you on the earth is a dwelling place﴾. If settlement on the earth had come about only through the second descent, then mention of His saying, ﴿And for you on the earth is a dwelling place and provision﴾ [al-Baqarah: 36] would have been more appropriate right after the second descent.

The other: He said in the second descent, ﴿Go down from it﴾, and the pronoun in ﴿from it﴾ refers to the Garden. That requires that the second descent also be from the Garden.

The second explanation: the repetition is for emphasis. In my view, there is a third explanation stronger than these two: when Adam and Eve committed the lapse, they were commanded to descend, and then they repented after the command to descend. It came into their hearts that since the command to descend was because of the lapse, then after repentance the command to descend should no longer remain. So God, exalted is He, repeated the command to descend a second time, so that they would know that the command to descend was not a punishment for committing the lapse, to end when the lapse ended. Rather, the command to descend remains after repentance, because the command to it was the fulfillment of the earlier promise in His saying, ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successive authority﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30]. If it is asked: what is the answer to the first condition? We say: the second condition together with its answer, as when you say: "If you come to me, then if I am able, I will treat you well."

**Second issue:** It is related in reports that Adam, peace be upon him, was sent down in India, Eve in Jeddah, Iblis in a place near Basra at a distance of miles, and the serpent in Isfahan.

**Third issue:** Regarding "guidance" (al-huda) there are several meanings:

The first: what is meant by it is every indication and clarification, so it includes the proof of reason and every speech sent down to a prophet. It also points to the greatness of God's blessing upon Adam and Eve, as if He said: "Even though I have sent you down from the Garden to the earth, I have bestowed upon you what will lead you once more to the Garden, with the everlasting eternity that never ends." Al-Hasan said:

[p. 26 continued]
When Adam, peace be upon him, was sent down to the earth, God, exalted is He, revealed to him: "O Adam, there are four qualities in which lies the whole matter for you and your offspring: one is for Me, one is for you, one is between Me and you, and one is between you and the people. As for the one for Me: you worship Me and do not associate anything with Me. As for the one for you: when you act, you receive your reward. As for the one between Me and you: upon you is supplication and upon Me is the answering. As for the one between you and the people: that you keep company with them in the way you would like them to keep company with you."

The second: what is related from Abu al-'Aliyah, that what is meant by guidance is the prophets. This holds only if the addressees in His saying, ﴿if guidance comes to you from Me﴾, are other than Adam and his descendants. In sum, this interpretation requires restricting the addressees to the descendants of Adam, and restricting guidance to a specific kind, namely the prophets, without any evidence supporting this restriction.

**Fourth issue:** He, exalted is He, made clear that whoever follows His guidance in truth, in knowledge and in action, by undertaking what is obligatory and refraining from what is forbidden, will arrive at a state in which there is no fear and no grief. This sentence, despite its brevity, gathers many meanings. His saying ﴿if guidance comes to you from Me﴾ includes the bestowal of all rational and revealed proofs, the additions of clarification, and everything without which this cannot be complete, such as reason and the means of capability. His saying ﴿whoever follows My guidance﴾ comprises reflecting on the proofs in their proper manner, considering them, deducing knowledge from them and acting upon them, and this encompasses all the obligations. His saying ﴿there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve﴾ comprises all that God, exalted is He, has prepared for His friends, because the removal of fear includes safety from all calamities, and the removal of grief requires attaining every pleasure and desire. He put the absence of fear before the absence of grief, because the removal of what is undesirable takes precedence over the pursuit of what is desirable.

This indicates that the accountable person who obeyed God, exalted is He, will not be touched by fear in the grave, nor at the Resurrection, nor at the presence of the place of standing, nor at the flying of the books, nor at the setting up of the scales, nor at the Bridge, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will meet them, saying, "This is your day which you were promised."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 103]

Some of the theologians said: just as the horrors of the Resurrection reach the disbelievers and the wicked, they also reach the believers, based on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from what she nursed﴾ [al-Hajj: 2]. Also, when those horrors are removed and they reach the Garden and God's good pleasure, what preceded becomes as if it had never been, and may even increase their enjoyment of the bliss they find. This view is weak, because His saying ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾ is more specific than His saying ﴿On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from what she nursed﴾, and the specific takes precedence over the general.

Ibn Zayd said: ﴿there will be no fear for them﴾ refers to what lies ahead of them; for nothing is more terrifying in the heart of one who dies than what comes after death, so God, exalted is He, granted them security from it. Then He consoled them concerning the world, saying: ﴿nor will they grieve﴾ over what they left behind after their death in this world.

If it is objected that His saying ﴿whoever follows My guidance, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve﴾ implies the absolute negation of fear and grief in this world and the Hereafter, and this is not the case, because they occur in this world for believers more than they occur for non-believers. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Affliction is reserved for the prophets, then for the friends of God, then for the best and then the next best."

Also, the believer cannot be certain that he has performed the acts of worship as they should be, so fear of falling short exists. Also, fear of a bad end exists. We reply: the context of the speech indicates that what is meant is the negation of these two in the Hereafter, not in this world. For this reason God reports about them that when they entered the Garden they said: ﴿Praise be to God who has removed from us grief; indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative﴾ [Fatir: 34], meaning: He removed from us what we were in, in this world, of fear and anxious concern lest the honour of God, which we now attain, should escape us.

**Fifth issue:** The Qadi (al-Qadi 'Abd al-Jabbar) said: God's saying, exalted is He, ﴿whoever follows My guidance, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve﴾ indicates several matters:

First: guidance may be established without there being actual being guided, which is why He said ﴿whoever follows My guidance﴾.

Second: the invalidity of the view that knowledge of the truths is necessary (darurah, knowledge that arises immediately without deliberation).

Third: that by following guidance, the Garden is deserved.

Fourth: the nullification of taqlid (blind imitation without evidence), because one who merely imitates is not a follower of guidance.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 2, verse 39:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs — those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾ When Allah promised the follower of guidance security from punishment and grief, He followed it with mention of the one for whom He prepared the everlasting punishment, so He said: ﴿But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs﴾, whether they are of mankind or of the jinn; they are the companions of the everlasting punishment.

As for the discussion of whether punishment is good or not, and, if it is good, whether it is good always or not, this has already been discussed in the explanation of His saying: ﴿And over their eyes is a covering, and for them is a great punishment﴾ [al-Baqarah: 7]. Here is the end of the verses that indicate the blessings which Allah has bestowed upon all the children of Adam. They indicate tawhid (the oneness of God) in that these blessings are originated things, so they must have an originator; and they indicate prophethood in that Muhammad (ﷺ) reported them in agreement with what existed in the Torah and the Gospel, without having learned them or studied under anyone; and they indicate the return (ma'ad) in that whoever was able to create these things at the beginning is able to create them again. And success is from Allah.

**The Discussion of the Particular Blessings Bestowed on the Children of Israel**

Know that when the Exalted and Glorified first established the proofs of divine unity (tawhid), prophethood (nubuwwah), and the return (ma'ad), He then followed them with mention of the general blessings bestowed on all of humanity. He then followed these with mention of the particular blessings bestowed on the forefathers of the Jews, in order to break their obstinacy and stubbornness by reminding them of past blessings, to win their hearts through them, and to draw attention to what indicates the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), in that these blessings are a report of the unseen.

Know also that He, Glorified is He, first reminded them of those blessings in summary form, saying: ﴿O Children of Israel, remember My favour which I bestowed upon you, and fulfil My covenant; I will fulfil your covenant﴾. He made the command to believe in Muhammad (ﷺ) a consequence of this reminder, saying: ﴿And believe in what I have sent down, confirming what is with you﴾ (2:41). Then He followed this with mention of the matters that would prevent them from believing in him. Then He reminded them of those blessings again in summary form, a second time, saying: ﴿O Children of Israel, remember My favour which I bestowed upon you﴾, as a warning about the extent of their heedlessness. Then He added to this reminder a strong encouragement, saying: ﴿And that I preferred you over the worlds﴾, coupled with a strong warning, saying: ﴿And fear a Day when no soul will avail another soul at all﴾ (2:48), up to the end of the verse. After that, He proceeded to enumerate those blessings in detail.

Whoever reflects and is fair will know that this is the pinnacle of excellent arrangement for one who wishes to call to faith and to establish conviction in the heart of the listener. Having established this introduction, let us now speak about the exegesis (tafsir), with the help of Allah.

* * *

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O Children of Israel, remember My favour which I bestowed upon you, and fulfil My covenant; I will fulfil your covenant, and fear Me alone﴾ (2:40). Know that in it there are several issues:

**The first issue:** The exegetes agree that Israel is Ya'qub (Jacob), son of Ishaq (Isaac), son of Ibrahim (Abraham). They say that the meaning of Israel is "servant of Allah," because *Isra* in their language means "servant" and *El* means "Allah." Likewise, Jibril (Gabriel) means "servant of Allah," and Mika'il (Michael) means "servant of Allah." Al-Qaffal (may Allah have mercy on him) said: It has been said that *Isra* in Hebrew means "man," so it is as if it were said: "man of Allah." Thus His saying ﴿O Children of Israel﴾ is an address to the group of Jews who were in Medina in the time of Muhammad (ﷺ), from the progeny of Ya'qub (peace be upon him).

**The second issue:** The definition of a blessing (ni'mah) is that it is a benefit conferred out of kindness to another. Some say: a good benefit conferred out of kindness to another. They said: We added this because a blessing merits gratitude, and if it were ugly, gratitude would not be merited by it. The truth is that this condition is not valid, because it is possible for gratitude to be merited by kindness even if the act itself is forbidden, since the aspect that merits gratitude is different from the aspect that merits blame and punishment. So what prevents the two from being combined? Do you not see that the sinner merits thanks for his favour and blame for his disobedience? Why, then, should it not be the case here as well? Let us return to explaining the definition: as for our saying "benefit," it is because pure harm cannot be a blessing. As for our saying "conferred out of kindness," it is because if it were a benefit but the agent intended his own benefit and not the benefit of the one to whom it was done, such as one who treats his slave-girl well in order to profit from her, or who intends to lure him into harm and deceive him, such as one who feeds a poisoned sweet to kill him, that would not be a blessing. But when the benefit is conferred with the intention of kindness to another, it is a blessing. Having understood the definition of a blessing, let us derive branches from it:

**The first branch:** Know that everything that reaches us, by day and by night, in this world and the Hereafter, of benefit and of the averting of harm, comes from Allah, Exalted is He, as He said: ﴿And whatever blessing you have is from Allah﴾ (16:53). Blessings are of three kinds:

First: a blessing in which Allah alone is singular, such as creating and providing.

Second: a blessing that reaches us from another, in that He created it and created the benefactor, enabled him to bestow it, created in him the capacity and the motive to bestow it, granted him success in it, and guided him to it. This blessing, in reality, is also from Allah, Exalted is He. However, since He caused it to come through the hand of His servant, that servant is thanked. But the one truly thanked is Allah, Exalted is He. For this reason He said: ﴿Give thanks to Me and to your parents﴾ (31:14), beginning with Himself. And he (peace be upon him) said: "He who does not thank people does not thank Allah."

Third: a blessing that reaches us from Allah, Exalted is He, by means of our acts of obedience. This also is from Allah, Exalted is He, because had He, Glorified is He, not granted us success in acts of obedience, helped us in them, guided us to them, and removed the excuses, we would not have reached any of them. Thus it becomes clear from this explanation that all blessings are from Allah, Exalted is He, as He said, Glorified is He: ﴿And whatever blessing you have is from Allah﴾ (16:53).

**The second branch:** The blessings of Allah, Exalted is He, upon His servants cannot be counted or enumerated, as He said: ﴿And if you were to count the favour of Allah, you could not enumerate it﴾ (16:18). This is impossible because everything placed in us of benefits and pleasures from which we profit, and the limbs and organs which we use to bring benefit and repel harm, and everything Allah, Exalted is He, created in the world that gives pleasure and indicates the existence of the Creator, and everything found in the world by seeing which one is restrained from sins, which is countless, all of these are benefits. For a benefit is pleasure or what is a means to pleasure. All that Allah, Exalted is He, created is of this kind, because everything that gives pleasure is a blessing, and everything that gives pleasure and is also a means to averting harm is likewise. And that which is neither a source of present benefit nor a repeller of present harm is nevertheless fit to be used as evidence for the wise Creator, so it becomes a means to knowing Him and obeying Him, and these two are means to everlasting pleasures. Thus it is established that all of His creatures, Glorified is He, are blessings upon the servants. And since minds are incapable of enumerating what is in even the least of things of benefits and wisdoms, how then can one encompass everything in the world of benefits and wisdoms? By this the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And if you were to count the favour of Allah, you could not enumerate it﴾ (16:18) is established.

If it is asked: If blessings are unlimited, and that which is unlimited cannot be known with certainty by the servant, how then did He command them to remember them in His saying: ﴿Remember My favour which I bestowed upon you﴾? The answer is that they are unlimited in terms of their kinds and individual instances, but limited in terms of their genera, and that is sufficient for the reminder which yields knowledge of the existence of the wise Creator.

Know also that since it is established that the entitlement to praise, commendation, and obedience is realized only by conferring a blessing, it is established that He, Exalted is He, is the one deserving the praise of those who praise. For this reason He said, condemning the idols: ﴿Do they hear you when you call, or do they benefit you, or do they harm?﴾ (26:72–73). And He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And they worship besides Allah that which neither benefits them nor harms them﴾ (25:55). And He said: ﴿Is one who guides to the truth more deserving to be followed, or one who does not guide unless he is guided?﴾ (10:35).

**The third branch:** The first thing with which Allah bestowed blessings upon His servants is that He created them living. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were dead and He gave you life, then He causes you to die, then He gives you life again, then to Him you will be returned?﴾ (2:28), and ﴿It is He who created for you all that is on the earth﴾ (2:29), up to the end of the verse. This is clear that the root of all blessings is life, because He, Exalted is He, mentioned life first among the blessings, and then He mentioned all the other blessings following it. He mentioned them to the believers only to show that the purpose of the life of this world is the life of the Hereafter and reward. He also showed that all that He created is of two kinds: that which benefits and that which is benefited by. This is the view of the Mu'tazilah (the rationalist school). But Ahl al-Sunnah (the people of the Sunnah) said: Just as He, Glorified is He, created benefits, He also created harms, and no one has any objection against Him. For this reason He named Himself "the Benefiter, the Harmer," and He is not questioned about what He does.

**The fourth branch:** The Mu'tazilah said: Allah, Exalted is He, has bestowed upon the accountable both the blessing of this world and the blessing of religion, and He equalized them in the religious and worldly blessings. As for the religious blessings, it is because everything within His power of kindnesses (alutf, sing. lutf, divine favours that facilitate obedience) He has done for them, and what He has not done is not within His power, for if He were able to show a kindness to the accountable person which He did not do, the accountable person's excuse would remain. As for the worldly blessings, it is according to the Baghdadi Mu'tazilah alone, because in their view it is obligatory to maintain what is optimal (al-aslah) in this world; but according to the Basrian Mu'tazilah it is not obligatory.

Ahl al-Sunnah said: Allah, Exalted is He, created the disbeliever for the Fire and for the punishment of the Hereafter. Then they differed as to whether Allah has any blessing upon the disbeliever in this world. Some of them said: These few blessings in this world, since they lead to lasting harm in the Hereafter, are not a blessing upon the disbeliever in this world, for whoever places poison in a sweet does not count the benefit obtained from eating the sweet as a blessing, since it is a path to great harm. For this reason He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that the respite We grant them is good for themselves; We grant them respite only that they may increase in sin﴾ (3:178).

Others said: Even though He, Exalted is He, has not bestowed upon the disbeliever the blessing of religion, He has indeed bestowed upon him the blessing of this world. This is the view of al-Qadi Abu Bakr al-Baqillani (may Allah have mercy on him). This view is more correct, and the following points indicate it:

First: His saying: ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, that you may become righteous﴾ and ﴿Who made for you the earth a bed and the sky a canopy﴾ (2:21–22). Thereby He draws attention to the fact that obedience to Him is obligatory upon all because of these blessings, namely the blessing of creation and provision.

Second: His saying: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were dead?﴾ up to the end of it, and He mentioned this in the context of bestowing favour and explaining blessings. Had nothing from Allah, Exalted is He, reached them of blessings, this would not be valid.

Third: His saying: ﴿O Children of Israel, remember My favour which I bestowed upon you, and that I preferred you over the worlds﴾ (2:122). This is an explicit text that Allah, Exalted is He, bestowed blessings upon the disbeliever, since those addressed by this are the People of the Book, and they were among the disbelievers. Likewise His saying: ﴿O Children of Israel, remember My favour﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And when We delivered you﴾ (7:141), and His saying: ﴿And when We gave Moses the Book and the Criterion, that you may be guided﴾ (2:53). All of this is the enumeration of blessings upon the servants.

Fourth: His saying: ﴿Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, whom We had established on the earth as We have not established you, and We sent down the sky upon them in abundance﴾ (6:6).

Fifth: His saying: ﴿Say: Who delivers you from the darknesses of land and sea, when you call upon Him?﴾ (6:63) up to His saying: ﴿Then you associate others with Him﴾ (6:64).

Sixth: His saying: ﴿And We have established you in the earth and made for you therein means of livelihood; little are you grateful﴾ (7:10). And in the account of Iblis He said: ﴿And You will not find most of them grateful﴾ (7:17). Had there been no blessing from Allah upon them, this statement would have no benefit.

Seventh: His saying: ﴿And remember when He made you successors after the people of 'Ad and settled you in the land﴾ (7:74), up to the end of the verse. And He said, relating from Shu'ayb: ﴿And remember when you were few, and He multiplied you﴾ (7:86). And He said, relating from Moses: ﴿He said: Shall I seek for you a god other than Allah, while He has preferred you over the worlds?﴾ (7:140).

Eighth: His saying: ﴿That is because Allah would not change a blessing He had bestowed upon a people﴾ (8:53). And this is explicit.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 2, verse 40 (part 2 of 4):**

The ninth: His saying: ﴿It is He who made the sun a shining light and the moon a light, and determined for it stages, that you might know the number of years and the reckoning. God did not create that except in truth﴾ [Yunus: 5].

The tenth: His exalted saying: ﴿And when We let people taste mercy after adversity has touched them﴾ [Yunus: 21].

The eleventh: His saying: ﴿It is He who conveys you through land and sea, until when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice in it﴾ [Yunus: 22], up to His saying: ﴿Then when He delivers them, behold, they commit injustice in the earth without right﴾ [Yunus: 23].

[Page 31]

The twelfth: His saying: ﴿And it is He who made the night for you as a garment﴾ [al-Furqan: 47]. And His saying: ﴿It is He who made the night for you that you may rest therein, and the day giving sight﴾ [Yunus: 67].

The thirteenth: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and caused their people to alight into the house of ruin? Hell, which they will enter, and wretched is the settling place﴾ [Ibrahim: 28–29].

The fourteenth: ﴿It is God who created the heavens and the earth and sent down water from the sky and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you, and subjected to you the ships to run upon the sea by His command﴾ [Ibrahim: 32].

The fifteenth: His exalted saying: ﴿And if you should count the favor of God, you could not enumerate it. Indeed, mankind is grossly unjust and ungrateful﴾ [Ibrahim: 34]. This is explicit in affirming that favor (ni'mah) applies to the disbelievers.

Know that the disagreement on this question returns to terminology, because there is no dispute that these things, namely life, reason, hearing, sight, and all kinds of provision and benefits, come from God Exalted. The disagreement is only over whether such benefits, when they are followed by those everlasting harms, are called "favor" in common usage or not. It is well known that this is a dispute over mere wording. As for what proves that whatever the responsible person (mukallaf) does not find pleasant, God Exalted created it only so that it may be used for reasoning about the Creator and about His gentleness and kindness, then the following points apply:

First: His exalted saying in the surah beginning "Atā amru llāh" (al-Nahl): ﴿He sends down the angels with the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [al-Nahl: 2]. Thus God made clear that He sent the messengers only as bearers of good news and warners, and for the sake of calling to His oneness, to belief in His unity and His justice. Then He said: ﴿He created the heavens and the earth in truth; exalted is He above what they associate﴾ [al-Nahl: 3]. ﴿He created man from a sperm-drop; then at once he is an open adversary﴾ [al-Nahl: 4]. Thus He made clear that the origination of the servant, along with the disbelief in him, is among the greatest proofs of the existence of the Creator, namely his transformation from state to state: from being a sperm-drop, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh, until he reaches from his lowest state, which is being a sperm-drop, to his most noble state, which is being a clear adversary. Then He mentioned after that the aspects of His bounty, saying: ﴿And the cattle — He created them for you; in them is warmth and benefits, and from them you eat﴾ [al-Nahl: 5], up to His saying: ﴿It is He who sent down water from the sky for you; from it is drink, and from it are trees in which you pasture [your livestock]﴾ [al-Nahl: 10]. By this He refuted the Dahriyya (materialist deniers of a creator) and the followers of the natural causes (ashab al-taba'i'), because He made clear that the water is one and the earth is one, yet the colors, tastes, and smells differ. Then He said: ﴿And He subjected to you the night and the day﴾ [al-Nahl: 12]. By this He refuted the astrologers (munajjimun) and the people of the celestial spheres (ashab al-aflak), who argued from their movements and from their being subjected to one uniform course to the createdness of these spheres. Thus God Exalted, by these verses, established that everything in the world is created for the sake of the responsible persons, because everything in the world that is distinct from the essence of the responsible person either is something the responsible person finds pleasant and rests in, so that he gains joy from it, or bears for him some burden, or gives him a lesson. Such is the case of harmful bodies like snakes and scorpions, for by looking at them he recalls the kinds of punishment in the Hereafter, so he guards against them and uses them as a proof of the Greatest Benefactor. Thus it is established that none of His creatures falls outside these benefits. Then, Glorified and Exalted is He, He drew attention to the greatness of His bounty through these things at the end of these verses, saying: ﴿And if you should count the favor of God, you could not enumerate it﴾ [al-Nahl: 18].

Second: His exalted saying: ﴿And God presents an example: a city which was secure and tranquil, its provision coming to it in abundance from every place; but it denied the favors of God﴾ [al-Nahl: 112]. By this He drew attention to the fact that the favor reaching them requires that its denial becomes a cause of change (of their condition).

Third: His saying about the story of Qarun (Korah): ﴿And do good as God has done good to you﴾ [al-Qasas: 77]. And He said: ﴿Have you not seen that God has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and has completed His favors upon you, both apparent and hidden?﴾ [Luqman: 20]. And He said: ﴿Have you considered that which you emit? Is it you who create it, or are We the creators?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 58–59]. And He said: ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [al-Rahman: 30], repeatedly. Everything in this surah is among the favors, whether in religion or in this world. This is what relates to this topic.

* * *

**(The third question): On the favors specific to the Children of Israel.** Some of the knowers (ʿarifin) said: The servants of the favors are many, but the servants of the Benefactor are few. God Exalted reminded the Children of Israel of His favors upon them, and when the matter came to the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), He reminded them of the Benefactor, saying: ﴿So remember Me; I will remember you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 152]. This indicates the excellence of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) over all other nations.

Know that the favors of God upon the Children of Israel are many:

(a) He rescued them from the trial they were in from Pharaoh and his people, and replaced that for them with establishment in the land and deliverance from servitude, as He said: ﴿And We wished to confer favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them the inheritors, and establish them in the land, and show Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers from them that which they feared﴾ [al-Qasas: 5–6].

(b) He made them prophets and kings after they had been slaves to the Copts (al-Qibt). So He destroyed their enemies and made them inherit their land, homes, and wealth, as He said: ﴿Thus, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit it﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 59].

(c) He sent down to them the great Scriptures, which He did not send down to any other nation, as He said: ﴿And when Moses said to his people, "O my people, remember the favor of God upon you when He appointed prophets among you and made you kings and gave you what He had not given anyone among the worlds"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 20].

(d) Hisham narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: Among the favor of God upon the Children of Israel was that He saved them from the family of Pharaoh, and shaded them with clouds in the wilderness (al-tih), and sent down upon them manna and quails in the wilderness, and gave them the stone which was like a man's head, which supplied them with as much water as they wished, whenever they wished. When they had no further need of water, they lifted it, and the water was withheld from them. He also gave them a pillar of light to illuminate for them at night. Their heads did not become disheveled, and their clothes did not wear out.

Know that Glorified and Exalted is He reminded them of these favors for several reasons:

First: Among the favors are things that testify to the truth of Muhammad (ﷺ), namely the Torah, the Gospel, and the Psalms.

Second: The abundance of favors makes disobedience grave, so He reminded them of those favors so that they would beware of opposing what they were called to: belief in Muhammad (ﷺ) and in the Qur'an.

Third: The reminder of abundant favors creates shame about openly opposing.

Fourth: The reminder of abundant favors indicates that the Benefactor singled them out among all people with them, and whoever singles out someone with abundant favors, the apparent matter is that he will not remove them from them, since it is said: "Completing a kindness is better than beginning it." Thus, reminding of past favors induces hope for future favors, and that hope prevents openly opposing and quarreling.

If it is said: These favors were not upon the addressees, but upon their fathers. How then can they be favors upon them, and a cause of greater disobedience on their part? The answer has several aspects:

First: Had it not been for these favors upon their fathers, they would not have survived, and this progeny would not have come into existence. So the favors upon the fathers became as if they were favors upon the children.

[Page 33]

Second: Belonging to fathers whom God Exalted especially favored with the blessings of religion and this world is itself a great favor in regard to the children.

Third: When the children hear that God Exalted singled out their fathers with these favors because of their obedience and their turning away from disbelief and denial, the child desires this path, because the child is naturally disposed to imitate the father in good deeds. Thus this reminder becomes a motive toward occupying oneself with good deeds and turning away from evils.

* * *

As for His exalted saying: ﴿And fulfill My covenant; I will fulfill your covenant﴾, know that the covenant (ʿahd) is attributed to both the one who makes the covenant and the one with whom it is made. They mentioned two opinions regarding this covenant:

The first opinion: What is meant by it is everything God commanded without specifying some obligations over others. Then there are narrations about it. One of them: He made His making them know His favors a covenant upon them, from the perspective that they are obligated to be grateful for them, just as they are obligated to fulfill a pledge and a binding agreement. And His saying: ﴿I will fulfill your covenant﴾ means the reward and forgiveness. He made the promise of reward resemble a covenant, in that both share the quality that breaking them is not permissible.

The second: al-Hasan said: What is meant by it is the covenant which God took from the Children of Israel in His saying: ﴿And We raised up from them twelve leaders, and God said, "I am with you. If you establish prayer and give zakah..."﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 12], up to His saying: ﴿And I will surely admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 12]. Whoever fulfills to God His covenant, God fulfills to him His covenant.

The third, which is the opinion of the majority of the exegetes: What is meant is: Fulfill what I have commanded you of obedience and what I have forbidden you of sins, and I will fulfill your covenant, meaning I will be pleased with you and admit you into Paradise. This is what al-Dahhak related from Ibn ʿAbbas. Its verification is found in His saying: ﴿Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for Paradise﴾ [al-Tawbah: 111], up to His saying: ﴿And who is truer to his covenant than God? So rejoice in the transaction you have made, and that is the great triumph﴾ [al-Tawbah: 111].

The second opinion: the "covenant" refers to what God established in the earlier Scriptures concerning the description of Muhammad (ﷺ) and that He would send him. This is stated in Surat al-Ma'idah in His words: ﴿And God had certainly taken the covenant of the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:12], up to His words: ﴿I will surely remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:12]. In Surat al-A'raf He said: ﴿My mercy encompasses all things, so I will prescribe it for those who fear Me and give zakah and those who believe in Our signs. Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel﴾ [al-A'raf 7:156]. As for God's covenant with them, it is that He would fulfill for them what He promised: the removal of the burdens and shackles that were upon them, around their necks. He also said: ﴿And when God took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I have given you of Scripture and wisdom, and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him"﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:81], and so on. He also said: ﴿And when Jesus, son of Mary, said: "O Children of Israel, I am the messenger of God to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah and giving good tidings of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad"﴾ [al-Saff 61:6].

Ibn 'Abbas said: God made a covenant with the Children of Israel in the Torah that He would raise up from the descendants of Isma'il an unlettered prophet. Whoever follows him and believes in the light that he brings, that is, the Qur'an, I will forgive his sin, admit him to Paradise, and give him a double reward: one reward for following what Moses brought and what all the prophets of the Children of Israel brought, and one reward for following what Muhammad, the unlettered prophet from the descendants of Isma'il, brought. The confirmation of this is in His words: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it believe in it﴾ [al-Qasas 28:52], up to His words: ﴿They will be given their reward twice for what they endured patiently﴾ [al-Qasas 28:54].

'Ali ibn 'Isa used to say: the confirmation of this is in His words: [Page 34] ﴿O you who have believed, fear God and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double share of His mercy﴾ [al-Hadid 57:28].

Its confirmation is also what Abu Musa al-Ash'ari reported from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Three people will be given their reward twice: a man from the People of the Book who believed in Jesus and then believed in Muhammad (ﷺ), for him are two rewards; a man who disciplined his slave-girl, taught her well, then freed her and married her, for him are two rewards; and a man who obeyed God and obeyed his master, for him are two rewards."

There remain two questions.

First question: If the matter is as you say, how could a group of them deny it? The answer has two aspects.

First: this knowledge was present among their scholars through their books, but they were not numerous, so it was possible for them to conceal it.

Second: that text was a hidden text, not an clear one, so doubts and objections could arise concerning it.
